docs.title: ClusterObjectSet Ready Condition Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Rename the ClusterObjectSet (COS) health condition from Available to Ready and replace its overloaded reason set with specific, actionable reasons, without changing the ClusterExtension-visible roll-up behavior.

Architecture: COS is experimental-only. The COS controller (internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller.go) is the sole writer of the condition; common_controller.go in the operator-controller package is the sole reader, reconstructing the ClusterExtension Progressing/Installed conditions from it. We rename the condition type, split the catch-all Reconciling/Blocked reasons into specific ones, merge RollingOut+ProbeFailure into a single readiness reason, drop bundle-version/"revision" verbiage from messages, then regenerate the experimental CRD, manifests, and API reference docs.

Tech Stack: Go, controller-runtime, boxcutter (pkg.package-operator.run/boxcutter v0.14.0), gomock, testify, kubebuilder markers (controller-gen), bingo-managed tooling.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-cos-ready-condition-blueprint.md — the plan implements that blueprint; executors read both.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Experimental-only API. COS has no standard-channel CRD. The controller file carries //go:build !standard. No compatibility gate blocks the rename; there is no standard manifest/CRD to update.
  • API group / label prefix: olm.operatorframework.io for all reasons, labels, annotations.
  • Reason values are CamelCase machine identifiers; messages are complete sentences, capitalized, ending with a period (OpenShift convention). Avoid raw err.Error() jargon except in the transient Reconciling catch-all.
  • No bundle version, no "revision" verbiage in COS messages. Bundle version is a ClusterExtension concept; COS self-describes as "the object set"; per-object messages say "object(s)".
  • Determinism: any list interpolated into a message (secret names, phase names, per-object detail) must be sorted so the message does not churn across reconciles.
  • Generated files are committed. After API-marker/doc changes, regenerate with the project's make targets (bingo-managed tools) and commit the output. Never hand-edit generated CRD YAML, manifests/*.yaml, or docs/api-reference/olmv1-api-reference.md.
  • Do not touch internal/operator-controller/applier/boxcutter.go availableConditionAssertion — it asserts a managed Deployment's Available condition (appsv1.DeploymentAvailable), unrelated to the COS condition.
  • Commits: DCO sign-off (git commit -s). If opening a PR, title prefix ✨ (minor/compatible change). End commit messages with Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• CE condition type stays Available. The ClusterExtension's public contract exposes a condition named Available (both the top-level roll-up and each status.activeRevisions[].conditions[] entry — clusterextension_types.go:522). The reader currently copies the COS condition verbatim, including .Type (common_controller.go:84, :97), so a naive constant rename would silently flip the CE's condition to Ready. The reader must be decoupled: look up the COS Ready condition but re-emit onto the CE as Available. → Task 1 tests assert the CE emits type Available.
  • ClusterExtension roll-up equivalence. The resplit must preserve the CE Progressing/Installed reasons (messages are allowed to change — they flow through from the reworded COS messages via progressingFromAvailable at common_controller.go:248, and that is intended): ValidationFailed/ObjectCollision must roll up like the old Reconciling (CE Progressing=Retrying, Installed failure reason Failed); MutableReferencedSecret/DigestMismatch must roll up like the old Blocked (CE Progressing=False/Blocked). → Task 4 tests.
  • Deadline precedence vs. blocked. Blocked-class reasons (MutableReferencedSecret, DigestMismatch) must NOT be overridden by ProgressDeadlineExceeded; ObjectsNotReady/ValidationFailed/ObjectCollision/Reconciling MUST remain deadline-overridable. → Task 3 tests.
  • Empty per-object detail. When the revision is not complete but no per-object probe detail is available yet, ObjectsNotReady must emit the generic Objects are not yet ready., never 0 object(s) are not yet ready:. → Task 3 test.
  • completedAt stamped once. status.completedAt must still be stamped exactly once, on first AllObjectsReady, and never cleared/re-set. → Task 3 test.
  • Message hygiene / determinism. DigestMismatch must not leak raw digests; MutableReferencedSecret and DigestMismatch must list names sorted. → Task 3 tests.

• Step 1: Rename/rewrite the setter helpers

Replace setAvailableWithDeadline (:654-671), setRetryingConditions (:673-675), markAsAvailable (:677-685), markAsUnavailable (:687-695) with:

// setReadyWithDeadline sets the Ready condition to the supplied status/reason/message,
// unless the progress deadline has been exceeded — in which case it reports
// Ready=False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded instead.
func setReadyWithDeadline(cos *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet, status metav1.ConditionStatus, reason, message string, isDeadlineExceeded bool) {
    if isDeadlineExceeded {
        markNotReady(cos, ocv1.ReasonProgressDeadlineExceeded,
            fmt.Sprintf("The object set did not become ready within %d minute(s). Last status: %s", cos.Spec.ProgressDeadlineMinutes, message))
        return
    }
    meta.SetStatusCondition(&cos.Status.Conditions, metav1.Condition{
        Type:               ocv1.ClusterObjectSetTypeReady,
        Status:             status,
        Reason:             reason,
        Message:            message,
        ObservedGeneration: cos.Generation,
    })
}

// setReconciling reports a transient internal error on the Ready condition.
func setReconciling(cos *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet, detail string, isDeadlineExceeded bool) {
    setReadyWithDeadline(cos, metav1.ConditionFalse, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonReconciling,
        fmt.Sprintf("Encountered a transient error, retrying: %s", detail), isDeadlineExceeded)
}

func markReady(cos *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet, reason, message string) bool {
    return meta.SetStatusCondition(&cos.Status.Conditions, metav1.Condition{
        Type:               ocv1.ClusterObjectSetTypeReady,
        Status:             metav1.ConditionTrue,
        Reason:             reason,
        Message:            message,
        ObservedGeneration: cos.Generation,
    })
}

func markNotReady(cos *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet, reason, message string) bool {
    return meta.SetStatusCondition(&cos.Status.Conditions, metav1.Condition{
        Type:               ocv1.ClusterObjectSetTypeReady,
        Status:             metav1.ConditionFalse,
        Reason:             reason,
        Message:            message,
        ObservedGeneration: cos.Generation,
    })
}

                collidingObjs = append(collidingObjs, ores.String())
            }
        }

            l.Error(fmt.Errorf("object collision detected"), "object collision, retrying after 10s", "phase", i, "collisions", collidingObjs)

Remove the revVersion := ... line (:226) and the if rres.InTransition() { ... } block (:227-229). Replace the completion branch and the else branch (:232-300):

    //nolint:nestif
    if rres.IsComplete() {
        // Archive previous revisions
        previous, err := c.listPreviousRevisions(ctx, cos)
        if err != nil {
            return ctrl.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("listing previous revisions: %v", err)
        }
        for _, a := range previous {
            patch := []byte(`{"spec":{"lifecycleState":"Archived"}}`)
            if err := c.Client.Patch(ctx, client.Object(a), client.RawPatch(types.MergePatchType, patch)); err != nil {
                return ctrl.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("archive previous Revision: %w", err)
            }
        }

        markReady(cos, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonAllObjectsReady, "All objects are ready and pass their probes.")

        if cos.Status.CompletedAt.IsZero() {
            cos.Status.CompletedAt = metav1.NewTime(c.Clock.Now())
        }
    } else {
        var notReadyMsgs []string
        for _, pres := range rres.GetPhases() {
            if pres.IsComplete() {
                continue
            }
            for _, ores := range pres.GetObjects() {
                pr := ores.ProbeResults()[boxcutter.ProgressProbeType]
                if pr.Status == machinerytypes.ProbeStatusTrue {
                    continue
                }
                obj := ores.Object()
                gvk := obj.GetObjectKind().GroupVersionKind()
                notReadyMsgs = append(notReadyMsgs, fmt.Sprintf(
                    "Object %s.%s %s/%s: %v",
                    gvk.Kind, gvk.GroupVersion().String(),
                    obj.GetNamespace(), obj.GetName(), strings.Join(pr.Messages, " and "),
                ))
                break
            }
        }

        if isDeadlineExceeded {
            // Deadline wins; use the generic summary as the "last status" so the
            // reconstructed ClusterExtension ProgressDeadlineExceeded message is stable.
            setReadyWithDeadline(cos, metav1.ConditionFalse, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonObjectsNotReady, "Objects are not yet ready.", true)
        } else {
            sort.Strings(notReadyMsgs)
            msg := "Objects are not yet ready."
            if len(notReadyMsgs) > 0 {
                msg = fmt.Sprintf("%d object(s) are not yet ready:\n%s", len(notReadyMsgs), strings.Join(notReadyMsgs, "\n"))
            }
            setReadyWithDeadline(cos, metav1.ConditionFalse, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonObjectsNotReady, msg, false)
        }
        if hasDeadline && !isDeadlineExceeded {
            return ctrl.Result{RequeueAfter: remaining}, nil
        }
    }

    return ctrl.Result{}, nil

Add near determineFailureReason:

// isClusterObjectSetErrorReason reports whether a ClusterObjectSet Ready-condition
// reason represents an error (as the former single "Reconciling" reason did), which
// the ClusterExtension surfaces as an installation failure.
func isClusterObjectSetErrorReason(reason string) bool {
    switch reason {
    case ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonReconciling,
        ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonValidationFailed,
        ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonObjectCollision:
        return true
    default:
        return false
    }
}

Replace the Reconciling check (:153-156) and refresh the doc comment wording from "Available" to "Ready":

    // An error reason on the Ready condition indicates an error occurred.

    // conditions is an optional list of status conditions describing the state of the
    // ClusterObjectSet.
    //
    // The Ready condition represents the health of the object set.
    // True means all objects are ready; False means one or more objects are not
    // ready or the object set cannot progress; Unknown is the initial state, before
    // the first reconciliation has evaluated the object set.
    //   - True with reason AllObjectsReady: all objects are ready and pass their probes.
    //   - False with reason ObjectsNotReady: one or more objects are not yet ready.
    //   - False with reason ValidationFailed: the object set manifests failed preflight validation.
    //   - False with reason ObjectCollision: one or more objects are managed by another object set.
    //   - False with reason MutableReferencedSecret: a referenced Secret is not immutable.
    //   - False with reason DigestMismatch: resolved content changed after creation.
    //   - False with reason ProgressDeadlineExceeded: the object set did not become ready within spec.progressDeadlineMinutes.
    //   - False with reason Archiving: the object set is being archived.
    //   - False with reason Archived: the object set has been archived and its objects torn down.
    //   - False with reason Reconciling: a transient error prevented reconciliation.
    //
    // Rollout completion is recorded separately by status.completedAt.

docs.title: 2026 10 12 cos ready condition completion
docs.text:
let's review let# ClusterObjectSet Ready Condition Completion — Implementation Plan

For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Finish the ClusterObjectSet (COS) Ready condition vocabulary across four stacked PRs: introduce ObjectsNotReady (retire ProbeFailure), Archiving, and Superseded, and remove RetryableError.

Architecture: Each PR is one gh-stack branch on top of the previous, based on main. The COS controller computes the Ready condition in reconcile()/archive(); the ClusterExtension (CE) controller reconstructs its own Progressing/Installed conditions from the COS Ready reason in common_controller.go. Each PR changes the COS reason emission and the CE mapping together so the two never drift.

Tech Stack: Go, controller-runtime, boxcutter (pkg.package-operator.run/boxcutter@v0.15.0), gomock, testify, kubebuilder/controller-gen. Build tag containers_image_openpgp.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-cos-ready-condition-completion-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Reasons are Go string constants in api/v1/clusterobjectset_types.go (status-condition reasons, not CRD-enum validated). No CRD compat gate; COS is experimental-only.
  • After any change under api/v1/ or helm charts, run make manifests crd-ref-docs and commit generated artifacts (helm/olmv1/base/**/crd/experimental/*.yaml, manifests/experimental*.yaml, applyconfigurations/**, docs/api-reference/olmv1-api-reference.md).
  • Each PR must pass make test-unit and make lint before it is opened.
  • Message style: capitalized, complete sentence, terminal period. COS self-describes as "the object set"; per-object messages say "object(s)"; never mention bundle version.
  • Per-PR consistency pass (definition of done for every task): (1) rename vars/functions/methods that still reflect retired vocabulary; (2) update test names, t.Run case names, and assertion messages; (3) fold any newly added unit test into an existing table test where it fits; (4) update docs/draft/concepts/clusterobjectsets.md and docs/superpowers/specs/clusterobjectset-ready-condition.md to match the code as of that PR.
  • Commit style: title prefix per repo convention — ✨ minor/compatible, ⚠ breaking. DCO sign-off and the attribution trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• ObjectsNotReady deadline overlay: when the deadline is exceeded while objects are not ready, Ready must still relabel to ProgressDeadlineExceeded (not ObjectsNotReady). Covered in Task 1.
  • Superseded vs ObjectsNotReady precedence: a revision with ≥1 ActionProgressed object and probe-pending objects must report Superseded, not ObjectsNotReady. Covered in Task 3.
  • Superseded vs deadline precedence: ActionProgressed objects while the deadline is exceeded must report ProgressDeadlineExceeded (deadline wins over Superseded). Covered in Task 3.
  • Archiving → Archived in one reconcile: when teardown completes, the final reason must be Archived, never left on Archiving. Covered in Task 2.
  • First-reconcile transient error (no prior Ready): a transient error before Ready is ever set must leave the condition absent and must NOT make the CE report Installed=Failed. Covered in Task 4.

docs.title: ClusterObjectDeployment Controller MVP Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Make the ClusterObjectDeployment (COD) controller create a new ClusterObjectSet (COS) revision on template change and report rollout progress via its Progressing condition.

Architecture: The COD reconciler (in the object-controller binary, //go:build !standard) lists COS in its group via the .spec.group index, detects template changes with a SHA-256 hash stored as a label on each COS, creates a new typed COS revision (<cod>-<rev>) owned by the COD when the hash differs, and sets Progressing from the latest matching COS's completedAt. Requeues come from the existing Owns(COS) watch.

Tech Stack: Go, controller-runtime, k8s apimachinery meta/conditions, gomock not needed (fake client), godog for e2e.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-cod-controller-mvp-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• COD controller code is experimental-only: every new controller file carries //go:build !standard (match clusterobjectdeployment_controller.go).
  • API group / label prefix is olm.operatorframework.io.
  • Child COS naming is <cod-name>-<revision>; COS spec.group = cod.Name.
  • Label-value limit is 63 chars: the template-hash digest is hex(sha256(...)[:16]) = 32 chars.
  • COS spec.collisionProtection is +required; default to Prevent when the template omits it.
  • New COS are created with plain typed Client.Create; AlreadyExists is treated as success.
  • Status is written via the status subresource (Status().Update), only when it changed.
  • Reuse existing constants: ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentTypeProgressing, ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonNewClusterObjectSetProgressing, ...Progressed, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetLifecycleStateActive/Archived, labels.OwnerKindKey/OwnerNameKey.
  • E2e feature files go in test/e2e/features/ named cod_<feature>.feature, tagged @BoxcutterRuntime (Feature-level), run on the experimental cluster.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Template change to a mutable COS field (progressionProbes only). Must still produce a new revision (this is the whole reason for the hash approach). Covered by Task 1 hash-sensitivity test.
  • collisionProtection omitted in the template. Must become Prevent on the COS or the COS is rejected (required field). Covered by Task 1 collisionProtectionOrDefault + BuildCOS tests.
  • Requeue race / duplicate create (<cod>-<rev> already exists because revs was stale). Must not error the reconcile. Covered by Task 2 AlreadyExists test.
  • Latest active revision is Archived (or deleting). latestActiveRevision must skip it so a fresh revision is created, and nextRevisionNumber must still count archived revisions so numbers never repeat. Covered by Task 1 latestActiveRevision/nextRevisionNumber tests and Task 2 "archived latest" test.
  • COD under deletion. Reconcile must be a no-op (children cascade via owner ref); must not create a revision for a deleting COD. Covered by Task 2 deletion test.

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectdeployment_controller.go (Reconcile body, reconcile, listRevisions, createRevision, setProgressing) - Modify: cmd/object-controller/main.go (pass Scheme: mgr.GetScheme() to the reconciler) - Test: internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectdeployment_controller_test.go (extend existing controllers_test file)

Interfaces: - Consumes: all Task 1 helpers; ocv1.ClusterObjectSet.Status.CompletedAt (metav1.Time, .IsZero()), controllers.SetupIndexes (registers .spec.group), testutil.WithIndexes. - Produces: - func (c *ClusterObjectDeploymentReconciler) reconcile(ctx context.Context, cod *ocv1.ClusterObjectDeployment) error - func (c *ClusterObjectDeploymentReconciler) listRevisions(ctx context.Context, group string) ([]ocv1.ClusterObjectSet, error) — List by client.MatchingFields{".spec.group": group}, sorted ascending by spec.revision - func (c *ClusterObjectDeploymentReconciler) createRevision(ctx context.Context, cod *ocv1.ClusterObjectDeployment, revisions []ocv1.ClusterObjectSet, hash string) error — builds COS, controllerutil.SetControllerReference(cod, cos, c.Scheme), Client.Create, ignores apierrors.IsAlreadyExists - func setProgressing(cod *ocv1.ClusterObjectDeployment, status metav1.ConditionStatus, reason, message string) — meta.SetStatusCondition with Type=Progressing, ObservedGeneration=cod.Generation

  • Step 1: Write failing behavioral tests in clusterobjectdeployment_controller_test.go (table-driven, testutil.WithIndexes(t, fake.NewClientBuilder().WithScheme(testScheme), controllers.SetupIndexes).WithStatusSubresource(&ocv1.ClusterObjectDeployment{}).WithObjects(...).Build()), each calling (&controllers.ClusterObjectDeploymentReconciler{Client: c, Scheme: testScheme}).Reconcile(...):
  • no existing COS → a COS cod-1 is created with group=cod, revision=1, lifecycleState=Active, owner-ref controller=COD, template-hash label set; COD Progressing=True/NewClusterObjectSetProgressing.
  • existing cod-1 with matching hash label and completedAt set → no cod-2; COD Progressing=False/NewClusterObjectSetProgressed.
  • existing cod-1 with matching hash label and zero completedAt → no cod-2; COD Progressing=True/NewClusterObjectSetProgressing.
  • existing cod-1 with a different hash label (template changed) → cod-2 created with revision=2; Progressing=True.
  • existing cod-1 Archived (latest active = none) → cod-2 created (revision=2).
  • existing cod-1 already present when creating revision 1 (seed cod-1 but force the create path via a stale list) → reconcile returns no error (AlreadyExists tolerated). (Simplest: assert createRevision tolerates AlreadyExists by pre-seeding cod-1 and calling reconcile on a COD whose latest active has a mismatching hash so revision 2 is attempted; then separately unit-test AlreadyExists by seeding the exact next-revision name.)

  • COD with non-zero DeletionTimestamp → no COS created, no status change.

  • Step 2: Run tests, verify they fail — go test -tags containers_image_openpgp ./internal/object-controller/controllers/ -run ClusterObjectDeploymentReconciler_Reconcile -v → FAIL.

  • Step 3: Implement the Reconcile flow per the design's Reconcile/reconcile/createRevision/setProgressing pseudocode. Outer Reconcile: Get (IgnoreNotFound) → if !DeletionTimestamp.IsZero() return → DeepCopy → reconcile → if !equality.Semantic.DeepEqual(existing.Status, reconciled.Status) then Status().Update, joining errors. reconcile: list revisions → hash → latestActive → create-or-noop → setProgressing. Add imports (crypto/sha256, encoding/json, encoding/hex, apierrors, apimeta/meta, controllerutil, runtime, equality).

  • Step 4: Wire Scheme in cmd/object-controller/main.go — add Scheme: mgr.GetScheme(), to the ClusterObjectDeploymentReconciler{...} literal.

  • Step 5: Run tests, verify they pass; then go build -tags containers_image_openpgp ./... and golangci-lint run on the touched packages.

docs.title: operator-controller writes a ClusterObjectDeployment (PR 1) — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: On the BoxcutterRuntime path, make the operator-controller create and maintain one ClusterObjectDeployment (COD) per ClusterExtension instead of creating ClusterObjectSet (COS) revisions directly; the COD controller owns revision creation/rollout/retention.

Architecture: The Boxcutter applier renders objects, runs preflights, packs objects into content-addressed ClusterExtension-owned Secrets, and server-side-applies a single COD whose template carries the ref'd phases plus bundle-metadata annotations. The COD controller creates the COS revisions (copying those annotations onto each COS) and adopts any pre-existing COS in the group. ClusterExtension status derivation is unchanged in this PR — it still reads COS revisions by group, which now exist because the COD created them.

Tech Stack: Go, controller-runtime, server-side apply (applyconfigurations), gomock, envtest, Godog e2e.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-operator-controller-use-cod-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• All changes are confined to the BoxcutterRuntime feature-gated path. The Helm path (gate off, standard manifest) and its applier/status are untouched.
  • No standard-manifest e2e may be modified; all must pass unchanged. New/changed e2es are @BoxcutterRuntime-tagged and run on the experimental manifest.
  • API domain for all generated labels/annotations: olm.operatorframework.io (reuse keys in internal/shared/labels/labels.go).
  • Secrets are owned by the ClusterExtension, set at creation (no two-phase owner-ref patch).
  • COD name == ext.Name == COS spec.group.
  • After changing //+kubebuilder:rbac markers or Helm charts, run make manifests and commit the regenerated files.
  • Build tag for object-controller code: !standard. Build tag for image handling: containers_image_openpgp.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• contentFS == nil (catalog unavailable). Apply must keep the install healthy using the already-applied COD without generating a new template; today the COS path has an explicit nil branch. Owned by Task 5.
  • Pre-existing COS adoption without re-roll. When the new applier first writes a COD for an extension that already has COS revisions, a steady-state extension must not trigger a spurious new revision (template hash must match). Owned by Task 6.
  • Secret name collisions across extensions. Dropping the revision-name prefix must not let two extensions (or two bundles) with identical object content share a Secret in a way that breaks GC/ownership; names remain unique per owner. Owned by Task 1.
  • COD SSA ownership churn. Re-applying an unchanged COD via SSA must be a no-op (no generation bump, no new revision). Owned by Task 5.
  • Bundle annotations missing on COS. If the COD does not propagate bundle annotations to the COS, the unchanged CE status reader reports an empty installed bundle. Owned by Task 2.

docs.text:

docs.title: Task 1: Content-addressed, revision-independent Secret packing
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: internal/operator-controller/applier/secretpacker.go - Test: internal/operator-controller/applier/secretpacker_test.go

Interfaces: - Consumes: nothing new. - Produces: SecretPacker{ OwnerName, SystemNamespace } (field RevisionName removed). Pack(phases []ocv1.ClusterObjectSetPhase) (*PackResult, error) unchanged in signature. Secret names are fmt.Sprintf("%s-%x", p.OwnerName, <sha256-of-sorted-data>[:8]). Secret labels carry labels.OwnerNameKey (no RevisionNameKey).

  • Step 1: Write the failing test — in secretpacker_test.go, TestSecretPacker_NameIsRevisionIndependent: pack the same phases with two SecretPacker{OwnerName:"ext"} values and assert the produced Secrets[0].Name are equal and begin with "ext-"; assert Secrets[0].Labels has labels.OwnerNameKey=="ext" and no labels.RevisionNameKey.
  • Step 2: Run test to verify it fails

Run: go test -tags containers_image_openpgp -run TestSecretPacker_NameIsRevisionIndependent ./internal/operator-controller/applier/ Expected: FAIL (field RevisionName still referenced / name has revision prefix).

  • Step 3: Implement — remove RevisionName from SecretPacker; change secretNameFromData to prefix with p.OwnerName; drop RevisionNameKey from newSecret labels. Leave data-key hashing and gzip logic unchanged.
  • Step 4: Run test to verify it passes

Run: go test -tags containers_image_openpgp -run TestSecretPacker ./internal/operator-controller/applier/ Expected: PASS.

docs.title: Task 5: Rewrite Boxcutter.Apply to write a COD
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: internal/operator-controller/applier/boxcutter.go - Test: internal/operator-controller/applier/boxcutter_test.go

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 4 generator; Preflight.Install/Upgrade; CE owner reference. - Produces: Boxcutter.Apply(ctx, contentFS fs.FS, ext *ocv1.ClusterExtension, objectLabels, revisionAnnotations map[string]string) (bool, string, error) — signature unchanged. New behavior: 1. If contentFS == nil: if a COD for ext.Name exists, return (true, "", nil) (maintain current state); else return an error "catalog content unavailable and no deployment installed". 2. Else: generate COD + Secrets (Task 4); set the COD owner reference to ext; pick preflight mode (Install when ext.Status.Install == nil, else Upgrade) and run enabled preflights on the rendered objects; create the Secrets (owner ref = ext, ForceOwnership) before applying the COD; SSA-apply the COD (FieldOwner, ForceOwnership); return (true, "", nil). - Deletes: createExternalizedRevision, garbageCollectOldRevisions, latestRevisionNumber, the COS SSA-diff state machine, patchSecretOwnerReferences/ensureSecretOwnerReferences, and the ClusterObjectSetRetentionLimit/revision-naming logic.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test — TestBoxcutterApply_WritesClusterObjectDeployment: fake client; call Apply with a stub content FS and ext{Name:"ext"}; assert exactly one COD named "ext" exists with owner ref to the CE, its template phases use refs, and the referenced Secrets exist in the system namespace owned by the CE; assert no COS is created directly by the applier.
  • Step 2: Run test to verify it fails

Run: go test -tags containers_image_openpgp -run TestBoxcutterApply_WritesClusterObjectDeployment ./internal/operator-controller/applier/ Expected: FAIL (Apply still creates COS).

  • Step 3: Implement the rewrite per the Interfaces block. Keep Preflight invocation and shouldSkipPreflight semantics; replace state selection with the ext.Status.Install check.
  • Step 4: Write the failing test for the nil-content and unchanged paths — TestBoxcutterApply_NilContentUsesExistingCOD (COD exists → (true,...), none exists → error) and TestBoxcutterApply_UnchangedIsNoop (applying identical content twice does not bump the COD generation).
  • Step 5: Run tests to verify they fail, implement, and verify they pass

Run: go test -tags containers_image_openpgp ./internal/operator-controller/applier/ Expected: PASS (all applier tests).

  • Step 6: Commit — git commit -m "✨ apply a ClusterObjectDeployment instead of managing ClusterObjectSets"

docs.title: ClusterObjectDeployment Template Metadata Propagation — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Give the ClusterObjectDeployment template a generic metadata (labels + annotations) that the COD controller propagates verbatim onto every ClusterObjectSet revision it creates.

Architecture: Add spec.template.metadata to the COD API (orb-operator shape), then extend buildClusterObjectSet to clone those labels/annotations onto each COS, stamping the controller-managed template-hash label last so it always wins. TemplateHash already hashes the whole template (JSON-based DeepHashObject), so metadata folds into revision identity automatically; omitzero keeps metadata-less CODs unchanged.

Tech Stack: Go, controller-runtime, kubebuilder validation markers, godog (e2e).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-cod-template-metadata-propagation-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• API changes follow OpenShift + Kubernetes conventions (AGENTS.md): value types, omitzero for struct JSON tags / omitempty for maps, +optional, doc comments use lowercase JSON field names.
  • After API type changes run make generate manifests crd-ref-docs; validate with make lint-api-diff. Commit generated files.
  • olm.operatorframework.io/* prefixes stay in the OLM domain; template-hash label stays controller-managed.
  • Scope is additive and OLM-agnostic: no bundle/OLM concepts in the COD controller. Do NOT touch bundleAnnotationKeys or the operator-controller applier (they live on operator-controller-use-cod, not this branch).
  • MaxProperties=32 on both maps; annotation values ≤ 256 KiB (262144 bytes).
  • Must build on macOS and Linux.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Caller supplies a template-hash label in template.metadata.labels — the controller must override it with the computed hash, never let the caller's value win (covered: Task 2 override test).
  • Nil / empty template.metadata — created COS has only the template-hash label and no annotations; existing metadata-less CODs keep the same template hash (no re-rollout) (covered: Task 2 empty-metadata + hash-stability tests).
  • Metadata-only template change — must produce a different template hash so a new revision is cut (covered: Task 2 hash-differs test).
  • More than 32 labels or annotations — apiserver rejects via CRD MaxProperties (covered: Task 1 validation test).
  • Annotation value larger than 256 KiB — apiserver rejects via CRD CEL rule (covered: Task 1 validation test).

docs.title: Task 1: COD API — template.metadata field + CRD validation
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: api/v1/clusterobjectdeployment_types.go (add field to ClusterObjectDeploymentTemplate, add ClusterObjectDeploymentTemplateMetadata type) - Modify (generated, via make): api/v1/zz_generated.deepcopy.go, applyconfigurations/api/v1/*, helm/olmv1/base/object-controller/crd/**/*clusterobjectdeployments.yaml, manifests/*.yaml, docs/api-reference/olmv1-api-reference.md - Test: api/v1/validation_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: ClusterObjectDeploymentTemplate.Metadata ClusterObjectDeploymentTemplateMetadata (json metadata, omitzero); ClusterObjectDeploymentTemplateMetadata{ Labels map[string]string; Annotations map[string]string } (json labels/annotations, omitempty).

  • Step 1: Add the type and field

In api/v1/clusterobjectdeployment_types.go, add to ClusterObjectDeploymentTemplate: 

// metadata contains labels and annotations propagated verbatim to each
// ClusterObjectSet created from this template. Changes to metadata change
// template identity and therefore create a new revision.
// +optional
Metadata ClusterObjectDeploymentTemplateMetadata `json:"metadata,omitzero"`
and add the new type: 
// ClusterObjectDeploymentTemplateMetadata contains labels and annotations
// propagated to each ClusterObjectSet revision created from the template.
type ClusterObjectDeploymentTemplateMetadata struct {
    // labels is a set of key/value pairs propagated to each revision's metadata.
    // +optional
    // +kubebuilder:validation:MaxProperties=32
    Labels map[string]string `json:"labels,omitempty"`

    // annotations is a set of key/value pairs propagated to each revision's
    // metadata. Each value must be 256 KiB or less.
    // +optional
    // +kubebuilder:validation:MaxProperties=32
    // +kubebuilder:validation:XValidation:rule="self.all(k, size(self[k]) <= 262144)",message="annotation values must be 256 KiB or less"
    Annotations map[string]string `json:"annotations,omitempty"`
}

  • Step 2: Regenerate

Run: make generate manifests crd-ref-docs Expected: zz_generated.deepcopy.go, applyconfigurations, CRDs, manifests, and API ref docs update with the new field; no errors.

  • Step 3: Validate API conventions

Run: make lint-api-diff Expected: PASS (no kube-api-linter violations on the new type/field).

  • Step 4: Write failing CRD validation tests

In api/v1/validation_test.go TestValidate, add cases (following the existing ClusterObjectDeploymentSpec case shape at the defaultDeploymentSpec / expectError pattern): - valid: Template.Metadata with a couple of labels and a small annotation → no error. - invalid: Template.Metadata.Labels with 33 entries → error. - invalid: Template.Metadata.Annotations with one value > 262144 bytes → error (match on the CEL message substring 256 KiB).

  • Step 5: Run validation tests

Run: go test -mod=mod ./api/v1/... -run TestValidate -count=1 Expected: PASS (requires envtest, as the existing suite does).

  • Step 6: Commit
git add api/v1 applyconfigurations helm manifests docs/api-reference
git commit -s -m "✨ add template.metadata to ClusterObjectDeployment"

docs.title: COD/COS referenced-secret ownership Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Make a ClusterObjectSet own (as a non-controller GC anchor) the object-data Secrets its phases reference, so those Secrets are reclaimed by Kubernetes garbage collection when the COS is deleted — without the object-controller otherwise managing them.

Architecture: The COS controller, early in its reconcile, ensures a single additive non-controller ownerReference (to itself) on each referenced Secret of type olm.operatorframework.io/object-data. It is idempotent and deduped by owner UID, so it coexists with the operator-controller applier's existing Controller=true patching (no-op where that ref is already present) and is the sole mechanism for standalone COD/COS. No COD secret logic, no sweeper, no finalizer.

Tech Stack: Go, controller-runtime, Kubernetes ownerReferences GC, Godog (e2e), envtest.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-24-cod-cos-referenced-secret-ownership-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• OwnerRefs added by the object-controller are non-controller (Controller=false), additive-only, deduped by owner UID. Never modify or remove an existing ownerRef. Do not set BlockOwnerDeletion (avoids needing clusterobjectsets/finalizers perms).
  • Claim (adopt) every referenced Secret, regardless of type, so its deletion follows the COS. No type gate. (The object-data-only restriction is deferred to future work.)
  • Claim on Secret existence, independent of content validity — the claim runs before the immutability/content precondition gates so a mutable/malformed referenced Secret is still owned.
  • Secret namespace handling matches the existing code (resolveObjectRef / verifyReferencedSecretsImmutable use ref.Namespace verbatim).
  • The COD gains no secret logic; keep validateTemplateMetadata unchanged.
  • The operator-controller applier (internal/operator-controller/applier/) is not modified by this plan (CE side deferred).

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Empty-namespace ref: the claim must Get the Secret at the same namespace the rest of the reconcile uses (ref.Namespace verbatim); a mismatch claims the wrong/no Secret. → Task 1 test.
  • Secret not yet created: a referenced Secret absent at claim time must be skipped silently (no error, reconcile continues; resolveObjectRef reports it later). → Task 1 test.
  • Same Secret referenced by multiple phases/objects: claim exactly once (dedup refs), one ownerRef. → Task 1 test.
  • Non-object-data (e.g. Opaque) Secret referenced: adopted and GC'd just like any other (type-agnostic). → Task 1 unit test + Task 3 e2e.
  • Applier coexistence: a Secret already carrying a Controller=true ownerRef with the COS's UID must not get a second ref (UID-dedup no-op). → Task 2 envtest.

docs.title: Task 1: COS claims referenced object-data Secrets
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller.go (add claimReferencedSecrets, call it from reconcile, add RBAC marker) - Test: internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller_internal_test.go (package controllers, fake client — mirror TestVerifyReferencedSecretsImmutable) - Modify (generated): run make manifests after adding the RBAC marker

Interfaces: - Consumes: ocv1.ClusterObjectSetKind, ocv1.GroupVersion; the reconciler's c.Client and *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet (has .UID, .Name, .Spec.Phases). - Produces: func (c *ClusterObjectSetReconciler) claimReferencedSecrets(ctx context.Context, cos *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet) error — called from reconcile after the deletion check and before verifyReferencedSecretsImmutable. Owns every referenced Secret regardless of type, independent of content validity. Returns a non-nil error only on a transient Get/Patch failure; nil when all existing refs are claimed and missing refs are skipped.

  • Step 1: Write the failing unit tests

In the internal test file, add Test_ClusterObjectSetReconciler_claimReferencedSecrets (table or subtests), using fake.NewClientBuilder().WithScheme(scheme).WithObjects(...).Build() as in TestVerifyReferencedSecretsImmutable. Cases, each asserting the resulting Secret's OwnerReferences after calling c.claimReferencedSecrets(ctx, cos):

- "object-data secret gets a non-controller ownerRef to the COS":
    secret.Type=SecretTypeObjectData; cos references it.
    want: exactly one ownerRef {APIVersion: ocv1.GroupVersion.String(), Kind: "ClusterObjectSet",
          Name: cos.Name, UID: cos.UID, Controller: ptr.To(false)}; err == nil.
- "idempotent: re-running adds no second ref":
    call claim twice; want still exactly one ownerRef with cos.UID.
- "already owned by this UID (e.g. applier Controller=true) is left untouched":
    secret pre-seeded with ownerRef {UID: cos.UID, Controller: ptr.To(true)};
    want: still exactly one ownerRef, Controller still true (no second ref, not downgraded); err == nil.
- "non-object-data (Opaque) secret is also claimed":
    secret.Type=corev1.SecretTypeOpaque; want: one non-controller ownerRef; err == nil.
- "missing secret is skipped":
    cos references a secret that does not exist; want: err == nil (no change, no error).
- "same secret referenced by two objects is claimed once":
    two refs to the same name/namespace; want: exactly one ownerRef.
- "empty-namespace ref is resolved at ref.Namespace verbatim":
    secret created in namespace "" is addressed by a ref with Namespace: ""; want: claimed.
  • Step 2: Run the tests to verify they fail

Run: go test -tags "!standard,containers_image_openpgp" -run 'Test_ClusterObjectSetReconciler_claimReferencedSecrets' ./internal/object-controller/controllers/ Expected: FAIL (claimReferencedSecrets undefined).

  • Step 3: Implement claimReferencedSecrets

Add the method to clusterobjectset_controller.go. Dedup refs exactly as verifyReferencedSecretsImmutable does (a map[struct{name,namespace string}]struct{}). For each unique ref: c.Client.Get the Secret; on apierrors.IsNotFound continue; on other error return a wrapped error; if secret.Type != labels.SecretTypeObjectData continue; if any existing ownerReference.UID == cos.UID continue; else build the non-controller ownerRef (fields above, no BlockOwnerDeletion) and apply it with a strategic merge patch (patch := client.MergeFrom(secret.DeepCopy()); secret.OwnerReferences = append(secret.OwnerReferences, ownerRef); c.Client.Patch(ctx, secret, patch)).

  • Step 4: Wire it into reconcile

In reconcile, after the !cos.DeletionTimestamp.IsZero() early return and before verifyReferencedSecretsImmutable, add: 

if err := c.claimReferencedSecrets(ctx, cos); err != nil {
    return ctrl.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("claiming referenced Secrets: %w", err)
}

  • Step 5: Add the RBAC marker and regenerate

Add secrets update to the object-controller's kubebuilder RBAC markers (the COS controller already has get;list;watch on secrets). Run make manifests.

  • Step 6: Run the unit tests + build

Run: go test -tags "!standard,containers_image_openpgp" -run 'claimReferencedSecrets' ./internal/object-controller/controllers/ → PASS Run: go build -tags containers_image_openpgp ./... → succeeds

git add -A  # include regenerated RBAC manifests
git commit -s -m "✨ ClusterObjectSet owns its referenced object-data Secrets for GC"

docs.title: ClusterObjectDeployment adoption of existing ClusterObjectSets — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Make the ClusterObjectDeployment (COD) controller adopt (take controller ownership of) the ClusterObjectSets (COS) in its group, failing loudly when a COS is owned by a different controller.

Architecture: On each reconcile, before GC and rollout, the COD ensures it is the controller owner of every COS in its group (spec.group == COD.name). Orphans are adopted via controllerutil.SetControllerReference; a COS already owned by a different controller yields *controllerutil.AlreadyOwnedError, which the COD surfaces as Progressing=False / RevisionOwnershipConflict (and skips rollout). Ownership spans the full history (active + archived). Revision numbering already counts the whole group, so a freshly minted revision never collides with an adopted one.

Tech Stack: Go, controller-runtime (controllerutil), the object-controller COD controller, envtest, Godog (e2e).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-cod-adopt-existing-cos-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• The family is spec.group == COD.name, discovered via the existing clusterObjectSetGroupIndex (same index the COS uses for siblings). Include active and archived revisions.
  • Adoption uses the native controller reference (controllerutil.SetControllerReference(cod, cos, scheme)): orphan → set + Update; already COD-owned (same UID) → no-op, no Update (avoid write churn); different controller → *controllerutil.AlreadyOwnedError.
  • A different-controller COS is an anomaly (group membership is exclusive to one COD): the COD sets Progressing=False with reason RevisionOwnershipConflict (message naming the COS and its controller), skips rollout and GC for that reconcile, persists status, and requeues (the COS watch re-triggers when the conflict is resolved). It must not steal the COS and must not only log.
  • Ownership reconciliation runs before garbageCollectArchivedRevisions and reconcileRollout.
  • nextRevisionNumber already returns max(.spec.revision over the group)+1; do not change it — adoption placing orphans in the listed group is what makes it correct, resolving the TODO: revisit AlreadyExists handling under the adoption use-case in createRevision.
  • Scope is COD-side only: do not touch the migrator, secret ownership, or the COS controller's sibling discovery.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Different-controller COS in the group: COD reports Progressing=False/RevisionOwnershipConflict and does not roll out (not stolen, not log-only). → Task 1 test.
  • Mixed group (orphan + foreign): orphans are still adopted, and the conflict is still reported. → Task 1 test.
  • Already-COD-owned COS: no spurious Update (idempotent; avoids a reconcile hot-loop). → Task 1 test.
  • Archived orphan revision: adopted too (ownership spans history). → Task 1 test.
  • COS in a different group (spec.group != COD.name): never touched. → Task 1 test (and inherent to the group-indexed list).

docs.title: Task 1: Adopt group ClusterObjectSets (ensureRevisionOwnership) + conflict condition
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: api/v1/clusterobjectdeployment_types.go (add the reason constant) - Modify: internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectdeployment_controller.go (add ensureRevisionOwnership, a typed conflict error, wire into reconcile; drop the stale AlreadyExists TODO on createRevision) - Test: internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectdeployment_controller_test.go (uses codFixture, newCODClient, reconcileCOD, getCOS, progressing, revisionCOS)

Interfaces: - Consumes: clusterObjectSetGroupIndex; controllerutil.SetControllerReference, *controllerutil.AlreadyOwnedError; metav1.GetControllerOf; setProgressing; the revisions []ocv1.ClusterObjectSet already fetched in reconcile. - Produces: - ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonRevisionOwnershipConflict = "RevisionOwnershipConflict" in api/v1/clusterobjectdeployment_types.go. - func (c *ClusterObjectDeploymentReconciler) ensureRevisionOwnership(ctx context.Context, cod *ocv1.ClusterObjectDeployment, revisions []ocv1.ClusterObjectSet) error — adopts every orphan in revisions; returns a *revisionOwnershipConflictError (holding the offending COS name + owning controller) if any revision is owned by a different controller; returns a plain error on a transient Update failure; nil otherwise.

  • Step 1: Write the failing unit tests

Add tests driving reconcileCOD (which calls reconcile) with group COSes seeded via newCODClient. Use revisionCOS(n, lifecycle) for orphans (it sets Group == clusterObjectDeploymentName, no owner), and set OwnerReferences for the owned/foreign cases.

- "adopts an orphan revision in the group":
    seed revisionCOS(1, Active) (orphan). reconcile. getCOS("test-cod-1-1"):
    GetControllerOf == the COD (Kind=ClusterObjectDeployment, Name=test-cod-1, UID=cod.UID).
- "no-op when already owned by this COD" (no spurious write):
    seed a revision already controller-owned by the COD; reconcile via a client with a
    write interceptor counting Updates on ClusterObjectSet; assert zero Updates to that COS.
- "reports RevisionOwnershipConflict when a group revision is owned by a different controller":
    seed revisionCOS(1, Active) with a controller ownerRef to a foreign owner (different UID/Kind).
    reconcile. progressing(): Status=False, Reason=RevisionOwnershipConflict. And no new revision
    is created (getCOS("test-cod-1-2") absent) — rollout was skipped.
- "adopts orphans even when another group revision is foreign-owned":
    seed orphan revisionCOS(1) + foreign-owned revisionCOS(2). reconcile.
    getCOS("...-1") is COD-owned; progressing() == False/RevisionOwnershipConflict.
- "adopts an archived orphan revision":
    seed revisionCOS(1, Archived) (orphan). reconcile. getCOS is COD-owned.
- "ignores a ClusterObjectSet in a different group":
    seed a COS with Spec.Group="other" and no owner. reconcile. that COS is left orphaned
    (GetControllerOf == nil).
  • Step 2: Run the tests to verify they fail

Run: go test -tags "!standard,containers_image_openpgp" -run 'ClusterObjectDeploymentReconciler' ./internal/object-controller/controllers/ Expected: the new cases FAIL (no adoption happens yet; no conflict condition).

  • Step 3: Add the reason constant

In api/v1/clusterobjectdeployment_types.go, add alongside the other Progressing reasons: ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonRevisionOwnershipConflict = "RevisionOwnershipConflict".

  • Step 4: Implement ensureRevisionOwnership + the typed conflict error

In the controller: define type revisionOwnershipConflictError struct{ cos string; owner string } with an Error() method. Implement ensureRevisionOwnership: for each rev in revisions, if metav1.GetControllerOf(&rev) is the COD → skip; else controllerutil.SetControllerReference(cod, &rev, c.Scheme) and, if it returns *AlreadyOwnedError, remember a conflict (COS name + existing controller) and continue; otherwise c.Client.Update(ctx, &rev) (adopt). After the loop, return the remembered *revisionOwnershipConflictError if any; else nil. (Transient Update errors are returned immediately.)

  • Step 5: Wire into reconcile and drop the stale TODO

In reconcile, after listRevisions and before garbageCollectArchivedRevisions: 

if err := c.ensureRevisionOwnership(ctx, cod, revisions); err != nil {
    var conflict *revisionOwnershipConflictError
    if errors.As(err, &conflict) {
        setProgressing(cod, metav1.ConditionFalse, ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonRevisionOwnershipConflict, conflict.Error())
        return nil // skip GC + rollout; status is persisted by Reconcile; COS watch re-triggers on resolution
    }
    return err
}
Remove the now-resolved TODO: revisit AlreadyExists handling under the adoption use-case comment on createRevision (numbering already counts adopted revisions).

  • Step 6: Run tests + build

Run: go test -tags "!standard,containers_image_openpgp" -run 'ClusterObjectDeploymentReconciler' ./internal/object-controller/controllers/ → PASS Run: go build -tags containers_image_openpgp ./... → succeeds. Run make generate manifests; expect no diff (no API struct change, only a string const).

  • Step 7: Commit

git commit -s -m "✨ ClusterObjectDeployment adopts existing ClusterObjectSets in its group"

docs.title: ClusterObjectDeployment Progressing reasons Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Give the ClusterObjectDeployment Progressing condition a COD-level reason vocabulary that distinguishes a normally-progressing rollout from one impeded by the head active ClusterObjectSet, and surfaces what the user must do.

Architecture: reconcileRollout reads the head active revision's Ready condition reason and maps it onto the COD Progressing condition. Hard stalls (ObjectCollision, InvalidSpecification) report Progressing=False and short-circuit the deadline; PreconditionsNotMet reports Progressing=True (still retrying) and is governed by the deadline; all other states fall through to the existing default progressing branch. No ClusterObjectSet-side changes.

Tech Stack: Go, controller-runtime, apimachinery apimeta, Godog e2e.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-cod-progressing-reasons-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• COD is an experimental, cluster-scoped API; changes are COD-controller-side only. No ClusterObjectSet controller, migrator, or spec changes.
  • API domain for any generated label/annotation prefixes: olm.operatorframework.io.
  • The conditions field docstring is the CRD schema field description; after editing it run make manifests crd-ref-docs and commit the regenerated CRD YAMLs and docs/api-reference/olmv1-api-reference.md.
  • No new Go struct fields are added, so no DeepCopy regeneration is expected; make verify must still pass.
  • Before opening the PR: make lint, make test-unit, make verify.
  • New reason strings (exact, verbatim): RevisionPreconditionsNotMet, RevisionObjectCollision, RevisionInvalidSpecification.
  • True/False mapping (fixed): InvalidSpecification→False, ObjectCollision→False, PreconditionsNotMet→True.
  • Ordering (fixed): hard stalls are evaluated before the deadline; PreconditionsNotMet after the deadline.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Head revision has no Ready condition yet (freshly created COS): must fall through to Progressing=True / NewClusterObjectSetProgressing, never a false hard stall. Pinned in Task 2.
  • Unrecognized / future head-revision Ready reason (e.g. Pending, ObjectsNotReady, or a reason added later): must fall through to the default progressing branch. Pinned in Task 2.
  • Hard stall arriving after the deadline has elapsed: ObjectCollision / InvalidSpecification must still report their stall reason, not ProgressDeadlineExceeded. Pinned in Task 2.
  • PreconditionsNotMet after the deadline has elapsed: must report ProgressDeadlineExceeded (deadline governs the retrying state), not RevisionPreconditionsNotMet. Pinned in Task 2.
  • A completed revision that later reports ObjectCollision/InvalidSpecification: completion is historical and must still win (NewClusterObjectSetProgressed), the stall must not resurrect. Pinned in Task 2.

Add prose covering: Progressing is True with reason RevisionPreconditionsNotMet when the head active revision's preconditions (e.g. RBAC or a dependency CRD) are not yet met and the controller keeps retrying; False with reason RevisionObjectCollision when the head revision's objects are owned by another controller or already exist (the user must resolve ownership); False with reason RevisionInvalidSpecification when the head revision's objects are invalid (distinct from the deployment's own InvalidSpecification, which is set for invalid spec.template.metadata before a revision exists). Keep the existing sentences for the other reasons.

docs.text:

Interfaces: - Consumes: reason consts from Task 1; existing setProgressing(cod, status, reason, message), latestActiveRevision, durationUntilDeploymentDeadline, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetTypeReady, and the COS reason consts ClusterObjectSetReasonInvalidSpecification/ObjectCollision/PreconditionsNotMet. - Produces: unexported helper headRevisionReadyReason(cos *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet) string returning the head revision's Ready condition reason, or "" when absent. The COD message is COD-owned generic text naming the revision (decision 4), not the COS message.

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests. Add a test helper setRevisionReadyReason(t, c, cosName, reason) (sets the named COS's Ready condition to status=False, reason=<reason> with a non-empty message) alongside the existing expireRevisionDeadline/getCOS helpers. Then add cases to the tabular test:
{
    name:       "head revision ObjectCollision reports RevisionObjectCollision and is not progressing",
    prep:       func(t *testing.T, c client.Client, cosName string) { setRevisionReadyReason(t, c, cosName, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonObjectCollision) },
    wantStatus: metav1.ConditionFalse,
    wantReason: ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonRevisionObjectCollision,
},
{
    name:       "head revision InvalidSpecification reports RevisionInvalidSpecification and is not progressing",
    prep:       func(t *testing.T, c client.Client, cosName string) { setRevisionReadyReason(t, c, cosName, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonInvalidSpecification) },
    wantStatus: metav1.ConditionFalse,
    wantReason: ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonRevisionInvalidSpecification,
},
{
    name:       "head revision PreconditionsNotMet reports RevisionPreconditionsNotMet and keeps progressing",
    prep:       func(t *testing.T, c client.Client, cosName string) { setRevisionReadyReason(t, c, cosName, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonPreconditionsNotMet) },
    wantStatus: metav1.ConditionTrue,
    wantReason: ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonRevisionPreconditionsNotMet,
},
{
    name:       "head revision with no Ready condition falls through to NewClusterObjectSetProgressing",
    prep:       nil, // default fixture COS has no Ready condition
    wantStatus: metav1.ConditionTrue,
    wantReason: ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonNewClusterObjectSetProgressing,
},
{
    name:       "head revision with unrecognized Ready reason falls through to NewClusterObjectSetProgressing",
    prep:       func(t *testing.T, c client.Client, cosName string) { setRevisionReadyReason(t, c, cosName, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonObjectsNotReady) },
    wantStatus: metav1.ConditionTrue,
    wantReason: ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonNewClusterObjectSetProgressing,
},
{
    name: "completed revision that also reports ObjectCollision still reports Progressed",
    prep: func(t *testing.T, c client.Client, cosName string) {
        setRevisionReadyReason(t, c, cosName, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonObjectCollision)
        cos, ok := getCOS(t, c, cosName); require.True(t, ok)
        cos.Status.CompletedAt = metav1.Now()
        require.NoError(t, c.Status().Update(t.Context(), cos))
    },
    wantStatus: metav1.ConditionFalse,
    wantReason: ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonNewClusterObjectSetProgressed,
},

Add a message-substring assertion to at least the PreconditionsNotMet, ObjectCollision, and InvalidSpecification cases proving the COD Progressing message is the COD-owned generic text that names the head revision and does not echo the COS message (decision 4): have setRevisionReadyReason write a distinctive COS message, then assert the COD message contains the revision name and does not contain that distinctive COS string.

In clusterobjectdeployment_deadline_test.go: - Add the two precedence cases: (a) deadline expired and head Ready reason ObjectCollision → ConditionFalse / RevisionObjectCollision (hard stall wins); (b) deadline expired and head Ready reason PreconditionsNotMet → ConditionFalse / ProgressDeadlineExceeded (deadline governs the retrying state). Reuse expireRevisionDeadline + setRevisionReadyReason. - Flip the existing invalid specification subtest in TestClusterObjectDeploymentReconcilerDeadlineWithoutCOSDeadlineCondition (~line 218): today a past-deadline COS with Ready=False/InvalidSpecification asserts ProgressDeadlineExceeded; under the new precedence it must assert ConditionFalse / RevisionInvalidSpecification. This is a behavior change to a currently-passing test, not a new case.

  • Step 2: Run the tests to verify they fail

Run: go test ./internal/object-controller/controllers/ -run ClusterObjectDeployment -v Expected: FAIL — new reason consts referenced but branches not implemented (wrong reason/status returned); compiles once Task 1 consts exist.

  • Step 3: Add the helper headRevisionReadyReason(cos *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet) string using apimeta.FindStatusCondition(cos.Status.Conditions, ocv1.ClusterObjectSetTypeReady), returning "" when the condition is absent.

  • Step 4: Implement the branching in reconcileRollout. After the !latest.Status.CompletedAt.IsZero() completed-branch and before the deadline check, evaluate hard stalls; after the deadline check, evaluate PreconditionsNotMet; otherwise keep the existing default. The COD message is COD-owned generic text that names the head revision and directs the user to inspect it — it must not echo the COS message (decision 4). Exact phrasing is the builder's call; the strings below are suggested defaults. Hard-stall branches return ctrl.Result{} (no bespoke timed requeue; the COS watch re-triggers). PreconditionsNotMet and the default branch keep the existing RequeueAfter: remaining when hasDeadline.

switch headRevisionReadyReason(latest) {
case ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonInvalidSpecification:
    setProgressing(cod, metav1.ConditionFalse, ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonRevisionInvalidSpecification,
        fmt.Sprintf("latest revision %q has an invalid specification; inspect the ClusterObjectSet for details", latest.Name))
    return ctrl.Result{}, nil
case ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonObjectCollision:
    setProgressing(cod, metav1.ConditionFalse, ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonRevisionObjectCollision,
        fmt.Sprintf("latest revision %q cannot take ownership of one or more objects owned by another controller or already present; inspect the ClusterObjectSet for details", latest.Name))
    return ctrl.Result{}, nil
}

remaining, hasDeadline := durationUntilDeploymentDeadline(c.Clock, cod, latest)
if hasDeadline && remaining <= 0 {
    setProgressing(cod, metav1.ConditionFalse, ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonProgressDeadlineExceeded, "latest revision exceeded its progress deadline")
    return ctrl.Result{}, nil
}

if headRevisionReadyReason(latest) == ocv1.ClusterObjectSetReasonPreconditionsNotMet {
    setProgressing(cod, metav1.ConditionTrue, ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonRevisionPreconditionsNotMet,
        fmt.Sprintf("latest revision %q is waiting for preconditions to be met; inspect the ClusterObjectSet for details", latest.Name))
    if hasDeadline {
        return ctrl.Result{RequeueAfter: remaining}, nil
    }
    return ctrl.Result{}, nil
}

setProgressing(cod, metav1.ConditionTrue, ocv1.ClusterObjectDeploymentReasonNewClusterObjectSetProgressing, "latest revision is progressing")
// existing requeue tail unchanged

Run: go test ./internal/object-controller/controllers/ -run ClusterObjectDeployment -v Expected: PASS (all new and existing cases).

docs.text:
• Ruling: Work on a feature branch in the existing operator-controller checkout instead of a separate git worktree — because the plan doc and superpowers workspace already live in this checkout's untracked tree and a worktree would separate them. Cost if wrong: branch shares the working dir with main; low risk since changes are additive test-only feature files.
  • Ruling: Per-task green verification (make e2e/<feature>) requires make experimental-e2e-setup (a KIND cluster), which the human acknowledged is out of band. Substitute per-task verification: static check that every Gherkin step in the new/edited feature files resolves to a step regex registered in test/e2e/steps/steps.go (catches the "undefined step" failure mode without a cluster). Cost if wrong: a step that resolves statically could still fail at runtime behaviorally; mitigated by matching wording to steps already used by passing cod_*.feature scenarios.

docs.title: Rulings (cont.)
docs.text: • Ruling: The plan/AC's "edit root deadline only -> no new revision" has no valid target: a root-level spec.progressDeadlineMinutes is pruned by the CRD (proved by TestClusterObjectDeploymentDeferredFieldsArePruned); the only deadline lives at spec.template.spec.progressDeadlineMinutes, which IS in the template hash and would cut a new revision. Substitute real non-hashed root fields: edit metadata.labels and spec.revisionHistoryLimit. Cost if wrong: if revisionHistoryLimit were ever folded into the template hash this scenario would start cutting a revision and fail loudly (acceptable it would surface a real semantics change).

docs.title: Standalone COD Lifecycle E2E (OPRUN-4794) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Close the remaining standalone ClusterObjectDeployment (COD) e2e gaps — idempotent reconcile, revision identity, multi-revision handoff, group isolation, and deletion teardown — by extending existing cod_*.feature files where topically aligned and adding focused new feature files otherwise.

Architecture: godog BDD e2e scenarios under test/e2e/features/, backed by step helpers in test/e2e/steps/. All assertions reuse existing registered steps — no new step helpers and no Go changes are required (verified against steps.go). Scenarios run against the experimental KIND cluster (object-controller enabled via the @BoxcutterRuntime tag).

Tech Stack: Go, cucumber/godog, controller-runtime client, KIND.

Spec: OPRUN-4794 ("Add standalone COD revision lifecycle e2e scenarios"). Companion tickets OPRUN-4849 (COS-only) and OPRUN-4795 (COD deadline/failure) are out of scope here.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Repo file cap: <=10 files across the branch; manual budget 4-6 files. This plan touches 3 feature files: cod_rollout.feature (modify), cod_handoff.feature (new), cod_lifecycle.feature (new). No Go/step changes.
  • All COD scenarios carry the @BoxcutterRuntime tag (object-controller is gated on it).
  • Scenario placeholders: ${NAME} is a per-scenario unique name; ${TEST_NAMESPACE} a per-scenario namespace. Derive extra names as ${NAME}-a, ${NAME}-1, etc.
  • Do not add or refactor steps. Every assertion must map to a step already registered in test/e2e/steps/steps.go.
  • New revision semantics (verbatim from controller reconcileRollout/templateHash): a new revision is cut iff templateHash(cod.Spec.Template) differs from the latest active revision's apps.kubernetes.io/template-hash label. The hash covers spec.template only. Root metadata and root spec.progressDeadlineMinutes are NOT hashed. Revision numbers are max+1 across the whole group including archived revisions and are never reused.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Idempotency false-pass under timing: asserting "no new revision" with a one-shot/eventual read can pass before a would-be successor appears. Pinned in Task 1 by holding the settled Progressing condition over a window (consistently reports Progressing as False with Reason NewClusterObjectSetProgressed for "15s") and then asserting ${NAME}-2 is not found — the existing idiom from cod_progressing_reasons.feature.
  • A->B->A reuse assumption: a reviewer may expect k8s-Deployment-style revision reuse; the controller cuts a fresh revision instead. Pinned by Task 1's A->B->A scenario asserting ${NAME}-3 exists and the COD owns 3 revisions.
  • Handoff UID identity: a shared managed object must keep its UID across the revision handoff (adopt, not recreate). Pinned by Task 2 via resource ... UID is remembered + keeps its UID.
  • Orphaned object cleanup: an object dropped from the template across a handoff must be deleted, not leaked. Pinned by Task 2 via resource ... is eventually not found.
  • Group isolation: one COD must not adopt another COD's revision. Pinned by Task 3 asserting each COD owns exactly its own revision (the owns N step verifies controller UID).

docs.text:

  • test/e2e/features/cod_handoff.feature (create): blocked-successor handoff, shared-object UID survival, dropped-object GC.
  • test/e2e/features/cod_lifecycle.feature (create): group isolation, COD deletion teardown.

Existing registered steps reused (verified in steps.go): resource is applied; resource "<k>/<n>" is removed; resource "<k>/<n>" is (eventually) not found; resource "<k>/<n>" UID is remembered; resource "<k>/<n>" keeps its UID; ClusterObjectSet "<n>" reports <T> as <S> with Reason <R>; ClusterObjectSet "<n>" has group "<g>"; ClusterObjectSet "<n>" is archived; ClusterObjectSet "<n>" is eventually deleted; ClusterObjectDeployment "<n>" owns <N> ClusterObjectSets; ClusterObjectDeployment "<n>" reports <T> as <S> with Reason <R>; ClusterObjectDeployment "<n>" consistently reports <T> as <S> with Reason <R> for "<dur>".

docs.title: COD Progress-Deadline Durability E2E (OPRUN-4795) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Validate the delivered COD revision-level progress-deadline contract (OPRUN-4791) with three focused e2e scenarios: deadline durability across a controller restart, post-completion health regression, and stall-and-recover without an extra revision.

Architecture: godog BDD e2e scenarios under test/e2e/features/, backed by step helpers in test/e2e/steps/. Reuses existing registered steps; adds one new step to restart the object-controller manager (the existing rollout restart step is hardcoded to the scenario namespace and cannot target olmv1-system). Scenarios run against the experimental KIND cluster (object-controller enabled via @BoxcutterRuntime).

Tech Stack: Go, cucumber/godog, controller-runtime client, KIND.

Spec: OPRUN-4795 ("Add COD stalled-rollout, creation-failure and restart e2e scenarios"), realigned to the OPRUN-4791 delivered contract.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Repo file cap: <=10 files across the branch; manual budget 2-4 files. This plan touches 2: cod_progress_deadline.feature (new) and test/e2e/steps/steps.go (one new step + registration).
  • All scenarios carry @BoxcutterRuntime; deadline scenarios additionally carry @ProgressDeadline (matching existing cod_progressing_reasons.feature tagging).
  • Deadline duration in tests: relax the CRD minimum with the existing step min value for ClusterObjectDeployment .spec.template.spec.progressDeadlineMinutes is set to 1, then use progressDeadlineMinutes: 1. This is a test-only CRD-validation relaxation, not a production timing override.
  • Delivered contract (verbatim, OPRUN-4791): deadline is one budget per revision from the COS metadata.creationTimestamp to status.completedAt; creation time excluded; phases share one budget and progress never extends it; timing derives from durable COS timestamps via an injectable clock so a restart reconstructs the same deadline; completedAt latches and ends deadline timing even after later health regressions; Available stays True while an active revision is Ready.
  • Controller target for restart: Deployment object-controller-controller-manager in namespace olmv1-system.
  • Do not refactor existing steps; add only.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Restart must not lose an exceeded deadline: a controller that anchored the deadline on process start (not the durable creationTimestamp) would, after restart, treat the revision as freshly observed and flip Progressing back to True. Pinned in Task 2 by restarting after expiry and asserting ProgressDeadlineExceeded holds consistently.
  • Post-completion deadline must stay disabled: once completedAt latches, a later health regression must not re-arm the deadline. Pinned in Task 1 by asserting Progressing stays NewClusterObjectSetProgressed while Available flips.
  • No spurious revision during a stall: a blocked revision must not cause a second revision to be cut. Pinned in Task 3 by owns 1 ClusterObjectSets after recovery.

docs.text:

  • test/e2e/steps/steps.go (modify): add RestartObjectController + one registration line.

Existing registered steps reused: OLM is available; namespace "<ns>" is available; min value for ClusterObjectDeployment <path> is set to <n>; resource is applied; resource "<k>/<n>" is removed; ClusterObjectSet "<n>" reports <T> as <S> with Reason <R>; ClusterObjectDeployment "<n>" reports <T> as <S> with Reason <R>; ClusterObjectDeployment "<n>" consistently reports <T> as <S> with Reason <R> for "<dur>"; ClusterObjectDeployment "<n>" owns <N> ClusterObjectSets; ClusterObjectSet "<n>" has group "<g>".

docs.title: Task 1: Post-completion health regression scenario
docs.text:
Files: - Create: test/e2e/features/cod_progress_deadline.feature (with this scenario first; later tasks append).

Interfaces: - Consumes: existing registered steps only.

  • Step 1: Write the scenario (@BoxcutterRuntime, Background: Given OLM is available). The deployment omits progressDeadlineMinutes (deadline disabled); readiness is gated by a FieldValue progressionProbe on a ConfigMap data.ready key that the template does NOT set, so boxcutter's SSA never owns it and the test can toggle it.

  • Scenario: Health regression after completion flips Available but not Progressing

    • Given namespace "${TEST_NAMESPACE}" is available
    • Apply a COD whose template has a single ConfigMap cod-health-cm (data k: v) and a progressionProbe: selector GroupKind {group: "", kind: ConfigMap}, assertions: [{type: FieldValue, fieldValue: {fieldPath: data.ready, value: "true"}}].
    • Assert ClusterObjectSet "${NAME}-1" reports Ready as False with Reason ObjectsNotReady (the probe fails until data.ready is set; confirmed reason in revision.feature's progressionProbe scenarios).
    • Set readiness: When resource is applied a ConfigMap cod-health-cm with data: {ready: "true"} (SSA-merges the extra key; the COS keeps data.k).
    • Assert ClusterObjectSet "${NAME}-1" reports Ready as True with Reason AllObjectsReady, ClusterObjectDeployment "${NAME}" reports Progressing as False with Reason NewClusterObjectSetProgressed, and ClusterObjectDeployment "${NAME}" reports Available as True with Reason Available.
    • Regress: When resource is applied the same ConfigMap with data: {ready: "false"}.
    • Assert ClusterObjectDeployment "${NAME}" reports Available as False with Reason Unavailable and ClusterObjectDeployment "${NAME}" consistently reports Progressing as False with Reason NewClusterObjectSetProgressed for "15s" (deadline stays disabled; completion is historical).

  • Step 2: Run; expect PASS

Run (needs experimental cluster): make e2e/cod_progress_deadline Expected: scenario passes. If a step is undefined, STOP and reword to the matching registered step (do not add tooling for this task).
