docs.title: ClusterObjectSet: single Ready status condition
docs.text: Date: 2026-09-25 Status: Design — pending review Scope: experimental only (ClusterObjectSet is an experimental API) Change class: ⚠ breaking API change (experimental channel)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Replace the two status conditions currently published on ClusterObjectSet (Available + Progressing) with a single Ready condition. Ready is the sole condition on the resource, with the following state table:

Status Reason When True Ready All phases complete False Incomplete One or more phases not yet complete False Blocked Requires manual intervention (see below) False Invalid Preflight validation error False Archived Teardown in progress or complete False ProgressDeadlineExceeded Not complete within the progression deadline Unknown ReconcileError Reconcile returned an error Unknown TeardownError Teardown returned an error Unknown InternalError Internal controller error

docs.title: Decisions captured during design
docs.text:
• Superseded is dropped. The original table included a Superseded reason ("objects adopted by a newer revision"). There is no equivalent in today's controller (a newer revision simply archives older ones on completion), and detecting it is net-new work. It is out of scope for this change and not added as a constant.
  • Object collisions map to Blocked. A collision (another controller owns a managed object) requires manual intervention, so it resolves to Ready=False/Blocked rather than a transient error.
  • Blocked folds in secret-immutability failures, resolved-phase content drift, and object collisions.
  • Probe failures fold into Incomplete. A failing readiness probe means a phase is not complete; there is no separate probe reason.
  • Deadline wins. For an active (non-archived) revision past its progressDeadlineMinutes, any not-yet-Ready state resolves to Ready=False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded, except Blocked, which continues to take precedence (preserving the existing "Blocked is more actionable" behavior).
  • The ClusterExtension keeps both Available and Progressing. To avoid churning e2e assertions now, the CE-side translator derives the CE's existing Available and Progressing conditions from the COS Ready condition (mapping in §4). The COS itself still exposes only Ready.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• No change to the standard (non-experimental) channel.
  • No Superseded detection.
  • No change to CompletedAt, ObservedPhases, or the progress-deadline rate-limiter mechanics — these already key off CompletedAt, not conditions.
  • No restructuring of the ClusterExtension's public condition set (still Installed + Progressing + deprecation types in conditionsets, with Available continuing to be emitted by the experimental mirror as today).

docs.title: 1. API changes (api/v1/clusterobjectset_types.go)
docs.text:
Remove condition-type constants ClusterObjectSetTypeAvailable, ClusterObjectSetTypeProgressing, and reason constants ClusterObjectSetReasonArchived/Blocked/ProbeFailure/ProbesSucceeded/Reconciling/Retrying.

Add:

// Condition Types
ClusterObjectSetTypeReady = "Ready"

// Condition Reasons
ClusterObjectSetReasonReady                    = "Ready"
ClusterObjectSetReasonIncomplete               = "Incomplete"
ClusterObjectSetReasonBlocked                  = "Blocked"
ClusterObjectSetReasonInvalid                  = "Invalid"
ClusterObjectSetReasonArchived                 = "Archived"
ClusterObjectSetReasonProgressDeadlineExceeded = "ProgressDeadlineExceeded"
ClusterObjectSetReasonReconcileError           = "ReconcileError"
ClusterObjectSetReasonTeardownError            = "TeardownError"
ClusterObjectSetReasonInternalError            = "InternalError"

Doc comment on ClusterObjectSetStatus.Conditions (currently lines 494-515): rewrite to describe only Ready and its status/reason combinations from the table above.

Printer columns (currently lines 564-565):

// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name="Ready",type=string,JSONPath=`.status.conditions[?(@.type=='Ready')].status`
// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name="Reason",type=string,JSONPath=`.status.conditions[?(@.type=='Ready')].reason`
// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name="Completed",type=string,JSONPath=`.status.completedAt`
// +kubebuilder:printcolumn:name=Age,type=date,JSONPath=`.metadata.creationTimestamp`

The Completed column uses type=string (not type=date) deliberately: kubectl renders type=date columns as a relative age (e.g. "3d"), whereas type=string against .status.completedAt prints the absolute RFC3339 timestamp. completedAt is omitted from the status until the revision first becomes ready, so the column is empty (<none>) until then.

docs.title: 2. Controller state machine (internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller.go)
docs.text:
Delete: markAsProgressing, markAsNotProgressing, markAsAvailable, markAsUnavailable, markAsAvailableUnknown, markAsArchived, setRetryingConditions, and the nonTerminalProgressingReasons map.

Add two helpers:

// setReady writes the single Ready condition unconditionally.
func setReady(cos *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet, status metav1.ConditionStatus, reason, message string) bool

// setReadyProgressing handles the "still working / erroring" states that are
// subject to the progress deadline. If the deadline is exceeded it overrides to
// Ready=False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded; otherwise it writes the given
// (status, reason). Callers pass Incomplete / Invalid / ReconcileError /
// TeardownError / InternalError. Blocked and Archived do NOT go through this
// helper (they bypass the deadline override).
func setReadyProgressing(l logr.Logger, cos *ocv1.ClusterObjectSet, status metav1.ConditionStatus, reason, message string, isDeadlineExceeded bool) bool

Exit-point mapping (replacing current calls):

Location (current line) Current call New call secret not immutable (139) markAsNotProgressing(Blocked) setReady(False, Blocked, …) build phases error (145) setRetryingConditions setReadyProgressing(Unknown, ReconcileError, …, deadline) observedPhases drift (153) markAsNotProgressing(Blocked) setReady(False, Blocked, …) create engine error (159) setRetryingConditions setReadyProgressing(Unknown, ReconcileError, …, deadline) archive: Free error (173) markAsAvailableUnknown(Reconciling) setReady(Unknown, TeardownError, …) establish watch error (185) setRetryingConditions setReadyProgressing(Unknown, ReconcileError, …, deadline) revision reconcile error (195) setRetryingConditions setReadyProgressing(Unknown, ReconcileError, …, deadline) preflight validation error (203) setRetryingConditions setReadyProgressing(False, Invalid, …, deadline) phase validation error (210) setRetryingConditions setReadyProgressing(False, Invalid, …, deadline) object collision (223) setRetryingConditions setReady(False, Blocked, …) in transition (230) markAsProgressing(RollingOut) setReadyProgressing(False, Incomplete, …, deadline) complete (250-251) markAsProgressing(Succeeded) + markAsAvailable(ProbesSucceeded) setReady(True, Ready, …) not complete, probe fail (288) markAsUnavailable(ProbeFailure) (folded) setReadyProgressing(False, Incomplete, …, deadline) not complete, rolling (290-292) markAsUnavailable + markAsProgressing setReadyProgressing(False, Incomplete, …, deadline) archive teardown in progress (317, 321) setRetryingConditions setReady(False, Archived, …) archive teardown complete (325 markAsArchived) Progressing/Available Archived setReady(False, Archived, …) delete: Free error (303) markAsAvailableUnknown(Reconciling) setReady(Unknown, TeardownError, …)

CompletedAt set (257-259) is unchanged. The IsComplete branch sets Ready=True/Ready and stamps CompletedAt exactly as today.

Note the not-complete branch collapses to a single setReadyProgressing(..., Incomplete, ...) call — the probe-failure message can be preserved in the condition message for debuggability, but the reason is always Incomplete.

docs.title: 3. Progress deadline
docs.text: No change to progress_deadline.go or durationUntilDeadline — they already derive the deadline from spec/metadata/CompletedAt. The deadline-override behavior (today inside markAsProgressing, lines 664-676) moves into setReadyProgressing: when isDeadlineExceeded is true, write Ready=False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded instead of the caller's (status, reason). Blocked paths bypass setReadyProgressing, preserving the "Blocked takes precedence over ProgressDeadlineExceeded" comment at line 136.

docs.title: 4a. common_controller.go — determineFailureReason (line 91)
docs.text:
Read the latest rolling revision's Ready condition instead of Progressing:

  • Ready=Unknown/* (ReconcileError/TeardownError/InternalError) → ReasonFailed
  • Ready=False/{Invalid, Blocked, ProgressDeadlineExceeded} → ReasonFailed
  • Ready=False/Incomplete or condition absent → ReasonAbsent

docs.title: 4b. boxcutter_reconcile_steps.go (lines 138-166)
docs.text:
Stop mirroring Available+Progressing verbatim. Introduce a translator that derives the CE conditions from a revision's Ready condition.

CE Available = the COS Ready condition retyped as Available. Status, reason, and message are mirrored 1:1 from Ready; only Type changes to Available. (Decision: "mirror COS Ready reason" — probe failures no longer produce a distinct ProbeFailure reason, so CE Available carries the Ready reason instead.)

CE Progressing is derived from Ready:

COS Ready CE Progressing True / Ready True / Succeeded False / Incomplete True / RollingOut False / ProgressDeadlineExceeded False / ProgressDeadlineExceeded False / Blocked False / Blocked False / Invalid False / InvalidConfiguration Unknown / {ReconcileError, TeardownError, InternalError} True / Retrying False / Archived not set by the translator (leave as-is)

CE Progressing reasons use the existing common_types.go constants (ReasonSucceeded, ReasonRollingOut, ReasonRetrying, ReasonBlocked, ReasonInvalidConfiguration, ReasonProgressDeadlineExceeded).

  • RevisionStatus.Conditions (per-revision, surfaced in ext.Status.ActiveRevisions[].conditions): mirror the single Ready condition. Update the RevisionStatus.conditions doc comment (clusterextension_types.go:519).
  • CE top-level: emit Available (retyped Ready) + derived Progressing from the installed revision, and derived Progressing from the latest rolling revision (as today).

Note: many CE Progressing assertions (e.g. InvalidConfiguration in install.feature) originate from CE-level reconcile logic (setStatusProgressing on apply errors), not the COS mirror, and are unaffected by this translator.

  • make manifests — helm base CRD (helm/olmv1/base/operator-controller/crd/experimental/olm.operatorframework.io_clusterobjectsets.yaml) and rendered manifests/experimental.yaml + manifests/experimental-e2e.yaml (printer columns + conditions description).

docs.text:
• internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller_test.go — rewrite all Available/Progressing assertions to Ready per §2.
  • internal/object-controller/controllers/progress_deadline_test.go — update deadline-override assertions to Ready=False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
  • internal/operator-controller/controllers/common_controller_test.go — update determineFailureReason cases to drive off Ready.
  • internal/operator-controller/applier/boxcutter_test.go — update mirror/ translation expectations.
  • test/e2e/steps/steps.go — ClusterObjectSetIsArchived (975-978) now waits for Ready=False, Reason=Archived. The generic ClusterObjectSetReportsCondition* step defs are type-agnostic and need no code change.
  • e2e feature files — all COS condition assertions must be rewritten (COS loses Available and Progressing). ~24 lines across:
  • revision.feature: :63,208 Available False/ProbeFailure and Message: → Ready False/Incomplete and Message:; :150+151, 326+327, 423+424, 519+520, 578, 710 Progressing True/Succeeded (+ paired Available True/ProbesSucceeded) → single Ready True/Ready; :471,548 Progressing False/Blocked → Ready False/Blocked; :640,709 Progressing False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded → Ready False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
  • update.feature: :318+319 → Ready True/Ready; :347+348 (Progressing True/RollingOut + Available False/ProbeFailure) → Ready False/Incomplete.
  • status.feature: :37,43 COS Available False/ProbeFailure → Ready False/Incomplete; :46 COS Available True/ProbesSucceeded → Ready True/Ready; :36,42 CE Available False/ProbeFailure → Available False/Incomplete (CE Available now mirrors the Ready reason).
  • install.feature: :373,407 COS Progressing False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded → Ready False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
  • CE Progressing assertions in recover.feature, install.feature, proxy.feature, update.feature (Retrying/Succeeded/RollingOut/ InvalidConfiguration/ProgressDeadlineExceeded) are preserved by the §4b translator + CE-level logic and need no change.

The test-experimental-e2e suite exercises the feature-file changes in §6.

docs.title: Design: Remove the Progressing condition from ClusterObjectSet
docs.text: Status: Draft — awaiting review Date: 2026-09-28 Scope: experimental channel only (ClusterObjectSet is experimental-only)

docs.title: Goal & intent
docs.text:
Remove the Progressing condition type from ClusterObjectSet (COS). Progress / retry / deadline semantics should be owned at the ClusterExtension (CE) layer; the lower-level COS API should expose only health (Available) and a done latch (status.completedAt).

This continues the direction of commit 85255103 ("Use completedAt in lieu of Succeeded condition on ClusterObjectSet"), which already removed the COS Succeeded condition in favour of completedAt.

docs.title: Decisions (agreed during brainstorming)
docs.text:
1. Approach 2 — express everything through Available. COS keeps its deadline and block-detection logic internally, but stops publishing a Progressing condition. The rollout/retry/block/deadline states that Progressing used to carry are folded into an expanded reason set on the single Available condition.
  2. Preserve the ClusterExtension condition contract. The CE's Progressing condition (types, reasons, semantics) must not change for users or e2e. The operator-controller now reconstructs the CE Progressing condition from COS Available + completedAt instead of mirroring COS Progressing.
  3. Fold Blocked / ProgressDeadlineExceeded into Available, accepting a small health-signal loss. These are rollout concerns, not health concerns, but to keep the logic in COS with only one condition left, COS sets Available=False with reason Blocked / ProgressDeadlineExceeded. In those states a blocked-but-running rolling revision no longer surfaces an independent health value. This is a documented, accepted deviation.
  4. Preserve current top-level CE Available mirroring. Today the operator-controller mirrors the installed revision's Available onto the top-level CE conditions (undocumented, untested). Keep that behavior to avoid any observable change.

docs.title: Background: what COS Progressing encodes today
docs.text:
internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller.go sets Progressing in five distinct ways:

Progressing state Trigger (call site) Available at that time True/RollingOut rres.InTransition() (L229); not-complete branch (L291) set separately (L287-289) or untouched True/Succeeded rres.IsComplete() (L249) — also sets completedAt True/ProbesSucceeded (L250) True/Retrying reconcile errors via setRetryingConditions (L144,158,184,194,202,209,222,651) Unknown/Reconciling — only if Available already exists (L652 guard) False/Blocked verifyReferencedSecretsImmutable (L138), verifyObservedPhases (L152) — terminal untouched (health preserved) False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded durationUntilDeadline inside markAsProgressing (L670-673) varies False/Archived markAsArchived (L727) Unknown/Archived (L728)

Key facts that make removal feasible:

  • status.completedAt already encodes "rollout complete" (== old Succeeded), and progress_deadline.go (deadlineAwareRateLimiter / durationUntilDeadline) computes deadlines from spec.progressDeadlineMinutes + creationTimestamp + completedAt — it does not read the Progressing condition. Requeue timing therefore needs no change.
  • Only the reporting of ProgressDeadlineExceeded (currently via markAsProgressing) needs a new home: it moves onto Available.

docs.title: Current condition mapping (COS → CE)
docs.text:
internal/operator-controller/controllers/boxcutter_reconcile_steps.go:

  • GetRevisionStates copies the full COS Status.Conditions into each RevisionMetadata, and classifies a revision as Installed iff completedAt is set, else RollingOut (L64-85).
  • ApplyBundleWithBoxcutter mirrors both Available and Progressing:
  • installed revision → top-level CE conditions + activeRevisions[0] (L139-150),
  • each rolling revision → its RevisionStatus.Conditions (L151-158),
  • latest rolling revision's Progressing → top-level CE conditions (L160-165).
  • On apply error, setStatusProgressing(ext, err) sets CE Progressing directly (L124-134) — unchanged by this work.

internal/operator-controller/controllers/common_controller.go:

  • determineFailureReason (L91-109) reads the latest rolling revision's Progressing reason; Retrying → CE Installed reason Failed, else Absent. This must switch to reading Available.

docs.title: 1. COS Available reason taxonomy (expanded)
docs.text:
api/v1/clusterobjectset_types.go — remove ClusterObjectSetTypeProgressing; Available becomes the single status condition with these (status, reason) tuples:

status reason meaning True ProbesSucceeded rolled out, all probes pass (paired with completedAt) False ProbeFailure rolling out, objects failing probes False RollingOut rolling out, not yet complete, no probe failures Unknown Reconciling reconcile error prevented observing probes (was Retrying) False Blocked terminal error, manual intervention required (new on Available) False ProgressDeadlineExceeded deadline exceeded before rollout (new on Available) Unknown Archived archived / torn down Unknown Migrated migrated, probes not yet observed

Notes: - Reconciling (already an Available reason) absorbs the old Retrying semantics. The L652 "only if Available already exists" guard is removed so first-reconcile retries are visible. - Deadline enforcement (if isDeadlineExceeded → ProgressDeadlineExceeded), currently centralized in markAsProgressing, moves into the Available-setting path for non-complete states.

docs.title: 2. COS controller changes
docs.text:
internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller.go:

  • Delete markAsProgressing, markAsNotProgressing, and the Progressing half of setRetryingConditions / markAsArchived.
  • Introduce a single helper for in-progress / not-complete states that applies the deadline check, e.g. markProgressing(l, cos, reason, message, isDeadlineExceeded) which sets Available=False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded when the deadline is exceeded, else Available with the supplied reason.
  • Rewire call sites:
  • L138 / L152 (Blocked): markAsUnavailable(Blocked, …).
  • L144/158/184/194/202/209/222 (Retrying): markAsAvailableUnknown(Reconciling, …) (unconditionally).
  • L229 / L291 (RollingOut): set Available=False/RollingOut (or ProbeFailure per L287-289) through the deadline-aware helper.
  • L249-250 (Succeeded): drop the Progressing line; keep markAsAvailable(ProbesSucceeded) + completedAt.
  • markAsArchived: keep Available=Unknown/Archived only.
  • progress_deadline.go: no change.

docs.title: 3. Operator-controller reconstruction (COS Available → CE Progressing)
docs.text:
internal/operator-controller/controllers/common_controller.go — add a pure helper:

// progressingFromAvailable derives the ClusterExtension Progressing condition
// for a revision from that revision's COS Available condition and whether it has
// completed (completedAt set).
func progressingFromAvailable(available *metav1.Condition, completed bool) metav1.Condition

Mapping:

input CE Progressing completed == true True/Succeeded Available reason Blocked False/Blocked Available reason ProgressDeadlineExceeded False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded Available status Unknown (Reconciling) True/Retrying otherwise (ProbeFailure / RollingOut / not-complete) True/RollingOut

Message is best-effort: reuse the Available condition's message. ObservedGeneration is rewritten to the CE generation, as today.

boxcutter_reconcile_steps.go — in ApplyBundleWithBoxcutter: - Mirror COS Available onto CE Available (top-level for installed; per-revision for all) exactly as today. - Replace every place that mirrored COS Progressing with a call to progressingFromAvailable(...) and SetStatusCondition: - installed revision → top-level CE Progressing + activeRevisions[0], - each rolling revision → its RevisionStatus.Conditions, - latest rolling revision → top-level CE Progressing.

common_controller.go — determineFailureReason: read the latest rolling revision's Available condition instead of Progressing; treat Available=Unknown/Reconciling (the new home of Retrying) as the error signal → ReasonFailed, else ReasonAbsent.

docs.title: 4. CRDs, manifests, docs (generated)
docs.text:
• api/v1/clusterobjectset_types.go: remove the Progressing printcolumn (L565); update the ClusterObjectSetStatus.Conditions doc block (L495-515) to describe only Available and its expanded reasons.
  • make manifests regenerates helm/olmv1/base/operator-controller/crd/experimental/…clusterobjectsets.yaml and manifests/experimental.yaml / manifests/experimental-e2e.yaml.
  • make crd-ref-docs regenerates docs/api-reference/olmv1-api-reference.md.
  • No Go struct shape change → zz_generated.deepcopy.go and applyconfigurations/** are unaffected (conditions remain []metav1.Condition).

docs.title: 5. Tests
docs.text:
• clusterobjectset_controller_test.go, clusterobjectset_controller_internal_test.go, progress_deadline_test.go: migrate assertions from Progressing to the expanded Available reasons (RollingOut, Reconciling, Blocked, ProgressDeadlineExceeded, Archived).
  • boxcutter_reconcile_steps_test.go, common_controller_test.go: assert the reconstruction produces the same CE Progressing tuples as before from COS Available inputs.
  • E2E test/e2e/steps/steps.go: ClusterObjectSetIsArchived (L975-978) waits on COS Progressing=False/Archived → change to Available=Unknown/Archived. CE Progressing steps (L684, L698-713) are unchanged (contract preserved).
  • Check hack/tools/migrate/ and internal/operator-controller/migration/ for any code that sets/reads COS Progressing; migrate to Available.

docs.title: Accepted deviations / risks
docs.text:
• Health loss in Blocked/DeadlineExceeded (decision 3): a blocked-but-running rolling revision no longer exposes an independent health value on Available; Available shows the rollout-blocking reason instead. Documented as intended.
  • Condition messages may differ byte-for-byte on the reconstructed CE Progressing (reasons and status match; messages are best-effort reused from Available). If strict message parity is required, it is achievable but adds coupling; not planned unless a test demands it.
  • Experimental-only surface, so no standard-channel CRD/manifest changes.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Moving deadline computation or block-detection to the operator-controller (that was Approach 1, not chosen).
  • Any change to the CE Progressing/Installed public contract.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• make generate manifests crd-ref-docs then make verify (generated code in sync).
  • make lint / make lint-api-diff.
  • make test-unit.
  • make test-experimental-e2e (COS is experimental).

docs.title: ClusterObjectSet Ready condition — reasons & messages blueprint
docs.text: Date: 2026-09-30 Status: Design blueprint (implementation deferred) Branch context: replace-available-with-ready

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Blueprint the target status-condition vocabulary for the ClusterObjectSet (COS) health condition, revisited from a UX perspective. Two changes frame this work:

  1. The condition is being renamed Available → Ready (see the ClusterObjectDeployment layering decision — COS gets Ready, the future ClusterObjectDeployment gets Available + Progressing).
  2. The reasons/messages are being revisited for clarity, actionability, and strict semantic boundaries so COS reads correctly when used standalone (outside ClusterExtension) and when its condition is propagated onto the ClusterExtension.

docs.title: Design decisions made during brainstorming
docs.text:
• Layering: rollout/progress reasons (RollingOut, ProgressDeadlineExceeded) stay on COS for now, but ultimately belong on ClusterObjectDeployment. ProgressDeadlineExceeded in particular is transitional.
  • Verbiage: drop "revision" and bundle <version> from messages. COS self-describes as "the object set" (matches the kind, standalone-safe, reads correctly when propagated onto ClusterExtension). Per-object messages say "object(s)". Bundle version is a CE concept and must not appear.
  • Split the overloaded Reconciling (currently ~11 distinct causes) into specific, actionable reasons; keep Reconciling only for truly transient internal errors.
  • Split Blocked (currently 2 causes) into two reasons with distinct remediations: MutableReferencedSecret (a referenced Secret is not immutable — a precondition/policy check) and DigestMismatch (current phase content digests no longer match those recorded in status.observedPhases — drift after creation, e.g. a referenced Secret was modified or recreated with different content).
  • Add Archiving for teardown-in-progress (distinct from generic transient errors), leading to the terminal Archived.
  • Message style: capitalized, complete sentence, terminal period; avoid raw Go err.Error() jargon except in the transient Reconciling catch-all.

docs.title: Ready = True
docs.text:
Reason Trigger Message AllObjectsReady Rollout complete — rres.IsComplete(): all phases done and every object passes its progress probe. Also stamps status.completedAt (once). All objects are ready and pass their probes.

AllObjectsReady was chosen over ProbesSucceeded (hardcodes the probe mechanism), Succeeded (implies terminal completion — that is now tracked by status.completedAt; Ready is a live health signal), and bare Ready (tautological). It is general, informative, and future-proof if readiness grows beyond a single progress probe.

docs.title: Ready = False
docs.text:
Reason Trigger Message (template) Notes ObjectsNotReady Not complete and deadline not exceeded: ≥1 object is not yet ready (progress probe pending/failing, or objects still being applied). Absorbs the former RollingOut + ProbeFailure — on the readiness axis these are one state seen at two instants (a pending probe already counts as not-True, clusterobjectset_controller.go:266). <N> object(s) are not yet ready:\n<per-object detail> (or Objects are not yet ready. before any probe reports) readiness-axis reason, symmetric with AllObjectsReady; per-object detail preserved ProgressDeadlineExceeded isDeadlineExceeded (time since start > spec.progressDeadlineMinutes) on any non-blocked path; wraps the would-be message as "Last status". The object set did not become ready within <N> minute(s). Last status: <msg> ⚑ transitional → moves to ClusterObjectDeployment.Progressing (the only remaining reason destined for COD) ValidationFailed A boxcutter classified preflight validation error — either the static revision check (rres.GetValidationError()) or the per-phase dry-run check (pres.GetValidationError()). See "Validation failure taxonomy" below for the exact causes. Object set manifests are invalid: <detail> / Phase <N> is invalid: <detail> split out of Reconciling (preflight + phase validation). Only classified validation errors land here; an unclassified dry-run failure (transient/network, or an APIStatus reason boxcutter does not treat as validation) returns a plain error → Reconciling. ObjectCollision ≥1 object reports machinery.ActionCollision. This is structurally a foreign owner: boxcutter only emits ActionCollision for unknown/foreign controllers (sibling-revision transitions become ActionProgressed, never a collision). No revision comparison needed on our side. Object(s) in phase <N> are managed by another object set:\n<list> split out of Reconciling MutableReferencedSecret ≥1 referenced Secret is not immutable — verifyReferencedSecretsImmutable fails (a referenced Secret has immutable != true). A precondition/policy check, not drift detection. Precedence: over the deadline. One or more referenced Secrets are not immutable. Referenced Secrets must set immutable: true; make them immutable or reference immutable Secrets. split out of Blocked DigestMismatch Current phase content digests differ from those recorded in status.observedPhases (verifyObservedPhases fails). Catches any post-creation content change — including a referenced Secret modified, or deleted and recreated with different content. Precedence: over the deadline. The resolved content for phase(s) <names> no longer matches the digest recorded in status.observedPhases. A referenced object source may have been deleted and recreated with different content. Create a new object set to apply the changes. split out of Blocked Archiving spec.lifecycleState=Archived and teardown in progress (teardown error, or owned resources not yet removed). The object set is being archived; removing owned objects. new — teardown in progress Reconciling Transient internal error: phase build, engine creation, watch establishment, revision reconcile, or cache free. Encountered a transient error, retrying: <err> now only transient/internal errors Archived spec.lifecycleState=Archived and teardown complete. The object set is archived. terminal

Precedence (when multiple triggers hold): MutableReferencedSecret / DigestMismatch (blocked) → ProgressDeadlineExceeded → ObjectsNotReady. Blocked wins because it is the most actionable; the deadline wins over per-object detail so the summarized "Last status" is reported. (Precedence is a guideline to finalize during implementation.)

docs.title: Ready = Unknown
docs.text: Trigger Message Before the first reconcile — the condition is absent (consumers treat a missing condition as Unknown). (none — condition not yet set)

docs.title: Mapping from current state
docs.text:
Current (Available) reasons and where they go:

Current reason Current message Target ProbesSucceeded Objects are available and pass all probes. AllObjectsReady (generalized; reworded to "ready") RollingOut Revision <version> is rolling out. merged → ObjectsNotReady ProbeFailure Object <Kind>.<gv> <ns>/<name>: <msgs> (joined) merged → ObjectsNotReady (add count summary; per-object detail kept) ProgressDeadlineExceeded Revision has not rolled out for <N> minute(s). Last status: <msg> ProgressDeadlineExceeded (reworded; transitional → COD) Reconciling raw err.Error() across ~11 sites split → ValidationFailed, ObjectCollision, Archiving, and a slimmed Reconciling Blocked raw err.Error() (2 causes) split → MutableReferencedSecret, DigestMismatch Archived revision is archived Archived (reworded/capitalized)

docs.title: Validation failure taxonomy (ValidationFailed)
docs.text:
Confirmed against boxcutter v0.14.0 (validation/ package). Two validators feed the two error surfaces the COS controller reads. ValidationFailed covers both.

A. Revision-level, static preflight — rres.GetValidationError() (*RevisionValidationError), from RevisionValidator.Validate → staticValidateMultiplePhases. Runs once, up front, no API-server contact:

  1. Static object-metadata violations (validation/metadata.go validateObjectMetadata): apiVersion empty, kind empty, or any of metadata.{uid,generation,generateName,finalizers,ownerReferences,resourceVersion} non-empty (manifests must not carry these).
  2. Invalid phase name (validatePhaseName) — not a DNS1035 label.
  3. Duplicate object across/within phases (checkForObjectDuplicates) — same GVK + namespace + name in more than one phase (PhaseObjectDuplicationError).

B. Phase-level, dry-run preflight — pres.GetValidationError() (*PhaseValidationError), from PhaseValidator.Validate (machinery/phases.go:198), run per phase right before that phase applies. Does everything in A for its objects plus live checks:

  1. Namespace-scope violations (validateNamespace, only on the namespaced validator, allowNamespaceEscalation=false): MustBeNamespaceScopedResourceError (cluster-scoped resource in a namespaced context), MustBeInNamespaceError (object namespace ≠ owner namespace), meta.NoMatchError (GVK not in cluster).
  2. API-server dry-run rejection (validateDryRun → DryRunValidationError): SSA dry-run (falling back to create-dry-run on NotFound) rejected with an APIStatus reason of Unauthorized, Forbidden, AlreadyExists, Conflict, Invalid, BadRequest, MethodNotAllowed, RequestEntityTooLarge, UnsupportedMediaType, NotAcceptable, or NotFound; plus the empty-reason case whose message contains "failed to create typed patch object".

Boundary: only classified errors become a validation error. In the phase validator, a dry-run failure that is not an ObjectValidationError (transient network error, or an APIStatus reason outside the list above) is errors.Join-ed and returned as a plain error — so it flows through the reconcile-error path (→ Reconciling), not ValidationFailed. This keeps ValidationFailed meaning "the manifests are structurally/semantically bad or the apiserver rejects them," while transient infra hiccups stay in Reconciling.

docs.title: Implementation notes (when this is picked up)
docs.text:
Primary file: internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller.go.

  • Rename the condition type constant ClusterObjectSetTypeAvailable = "Available" → Ready in api/v1/clusterobjectset_types.go:29; update the doc block (~497-509) and the printcolumn (~563). COS is experimental-only (no standard-channel CRD), so no compat gate blocks the rename.
  • Remove the dead ClusterObjectSetReasonRetrying = "Retrying" constant.
  • Retire the Blocked reason; add the new reason constants.
  • Drop revVersion := cos.GetAnnotations()[labels.BundleVersionKey] from the message paths (~line 226) — bundle version is a CE concept.
  • Merge the RollingOut (~228, ~295) and ProbeFailure (~293) paths into a single ObjectsNotReady reason; keep the per-object detail as the message, falling back to a generic line before any probe reports. Drop the bare in-transition RollingOut (~228) as a distinct reason.
  • Split setRetryingConditions call sites by cause:
  • preflight validation (~201) + phase validation (~208) → ValidationFailed
  • object collisions (~221) → ObjectCollision (foreign owner only — boxcutter emits ActionCollision solely for unknown/foreign controllers).
  • archive teardown incomplete (~324) → Archiving
  • phase build (~143), engine create (~157), watch (~183), reconcile (~193), cache-free (~171, ~307), archive teardown error (~320) → Reconciling
  • Split the markAsUnavailable(..., Blocked, ...) sites: referenced-Secret immutability check verifyReferencedSecretsImmutable (~137) → MutableReferencedSecret; resolved-phase digest drift verifyObservedPhases (~151) → DigestMismatch.
  • Update readers/tests: internal/operator-controller/controllers/common_controller.go (reads the condition to roll up CE status) and the _test.go files for both controllers. (NB: internal/operator-controller/applier/boxcutter.go asserts a managed Deployment's appsv1.DeploymentAvailable condition — unrelated to the COS condition; do not touch it.)
  • Keep the ClusterExtension Available condition — decouple it from the COS rename. common_controller.go currently copies the COS condition onto the CE verbatim, including .Type (setAvailableFromRevisionStates, setActiveRevisionsFromRevisionStates), so a naive rename would silently flip the CE's condition (top-level and status.activeRevisions[].conditions[]) to Ready. The CE contract (documented at clusterextension_types.go:522) must keep exposing Available. So: the reader looks up the COS Ready condition but re-emits onto the CE as a CE-owned TypeAvailable = "Available" constant (new, in common_types.go). This also keeps the CE contract stable across the future COS→COD transition (COD will own Available). The CE Progressing/Installed reasons are preserved; the CE Progressing message is allowed to change (it flows through from the reworded COS message via progressingFromAvailable) — this is intended.
  • Regenerate: make manifests crd-ref-docs (experimental CRD YAML, manifests/experimental*.yaml, docs/api-reference/olmv1-api-reference.md).

docs.title: Open / follow-on
docs.text:
• Superseded reason — DEFERRED (not in this plan; to be added later). A distinct reason for objects adopted by a newer sibling revision is out of scope for this iteration. The boxcutter research below is retained so it can be picked up when Superseded is added. Until then, a partial supersession surfaces as ObjectsNotReady (phase InTransition() == true). Engine support is already CONFIRMED (boxcutter v0.14.0) — boxcutter distinguishes a newer-sibling adoption from a foreign owner, so no revision-comparison logic is needed on our side:
  • OLM wires siblings via boxcutter.WithSiblingOwners(siblingObjs) (clusterobjectset_controller.go:491, from listSiblingRevisions).
  • machinery/objects.go:365-419: a newer sibling owning an object → newObjectResultProgressed → ActionProgressed; an unknown/foreign controller → newObjectResultConflict → ActionCollision. ActionProgressed has a single producer (that path).
  • When added, detect Superseded via per-object Action() == machinery.ActionProgressed, or phase-level HasProgressed() (all objects moved) / InTransition() (some moved) in machinery/phases.go.
  • Note: a partial supersession sets phase InTransition() == true, which drives the old revision to the in-progress state (ObjectsNotReady after the merge) — so when Superseded is added it must be evaluated before ObjectsNotReady.
  • When ClusterObjectDeployment lands: move ProgressDeadlineExceeded to COD.Progressing (the only remaining COS reason destined for COD, now that RollingOut is absorbed into the readiness reason ObjectsNotReady), and rewire ClusterExtension to observe COD (Available/Progressing) rather than reading COS directly in common_controller.go.

docs.title: ClusterObjectSet Ready condition — completion (stacked PRs)
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-12 Status: Design (approved decisions, pending spec review) Stack base: main (PR #2985 merged as f47aaefa) Builds on: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-cos-ready-condition-blueprint.md

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Finish the ClusterObjectSet (COS) Ready condition vocabulary started in the 2026-09-30 blueprint and the #2985 ValidationFailure consolidation. Four independently-reviewable, stacked PRs refine the remaining readiness reasons so the condition reads correctly standalone and when reconstructed onto the ClusterExtension (CE).

This is experimental-API-only. Reasons are Go string constants on the status condition (not CRD-enum validated), so no CRD schema/compat gate is involved; each PR still regenerates manifests, apply configurations, and reference docs for doc-comment/printcolumn churn.

docs.title: End-state vocabulary (after all four PRs)
docs.text:
COS Ready:

Status Reason Trigger True AllObjectsReady rres.IsComplete() — all phases done, every object passes its progress probe False Superseded ≥1 object adopted by a newer sibling revision (machinery.ActionProgressed) False ObjectsNotReady not complete, deadline not exceeded: ≥1 object still applying or probe pending/failing (absorbs the former RollingOut + ProbeFailure) False ObjectCollision ≥1 object reports machinery.ActionCollision (foreign owner) False ValidationFailure classified preflight/phase validation failure (from #2985; unchanged here) False Archiving spec.lifecycleState=Archived and teardown in progress False Archived archived and teardown complete (terminal) False ProgressDeadlineExceeded deadline exceeded; wins over the readiness reasons (unchanged) (prior reason) transient internal error — condition left untouched, error returned for backoff

Precedence (Ready=False, when multiple hold): ValidationFailure is reported first and is not overridden by the progress deadline (it wins because it is the most actionable). The remaining not-ready reasons — ObjectCollision, Superseded, ObjectsNotReady — are relabeled to ProgressDeadlineExceeded once the deadline is exceeded; below the deadline they rank ObjectCollision → Superseded → ObjectsNotReady. So the progress deadline intentionally overrides ObjectCollision (unlike ValidationFailure): past the deadline a collision reads as ProgressDeadlineExceeded. This asymmetry is a deliberate, documented choice, not a bug; see the living reference doc. Archiving/Archived are on the archival path and mutually exclusive with the active-rollout reasons.

RetryableError is removed entirely.

docs.title: Confirmed decisions
docs.text:
1. Superseded is partial. Fire as soon as ≥1 object has ActionProgressed, evaluated before ObjectsNotReady. A partial hand-off reads as superseded rather than masquerading as ObjectsNotReady.
  2. CE goes neutral on transient COS errors. With RetryableError gone, a transient COS error leaves Ready untouched and returns an error for backoff. CE no longer flips Installed=Failed or Progressing=Retrying for it; CE reflects the unchanged COS Ready reason (→ Absent / RollingOut). On a first-ever reconcile that hits a transient error before Ready is set, Ready stays absent (consumers read absent as Unknown). Accepted.
  3. Stack on main. #2985 has merged (f47aaefa); the four PRs stack on main rather than the old cos-ready-validation branch.

docs.title: PR decomposition
docs.text:
Each PR is TDD'd and self-contained: controller change + CE-mapping update in internal/operator-controller/controllers/common_controller.go + unit tests (both controllers) + make manifests crd-ref-docs.

Per-PR consistency pass (definition of done). After the functional change of each PR lands and tests pass, before opening the PR run a cleanup pass:

  1. Names: do any variable / function / method names still reflect a retired reason or old behavior (e.g. setRetryableErrorConditions, probeFailureMsgs)? Rename to match the new vocabulary.
  2. Test names/descriptions: do test function names, t.Run case names, and assertion messages still describe the old reason/behavior? Update them.
  3. Tabular folding: can any unit test added in this PR be folded into an existing table test (e.g. RevisionReconciliation, ForeignRevisionCollision) rather than standing alone? Fold where it fits the table's shape.
  4. Docs: update every doc the change touches — docs/draft/concepts/clusterobjectsets.md (status-condition tables) and the living reference docs/superpowers/specs/clusterobjectset-ready-condition.md (reasons, precedence, CE roll-up). Keep both in step with the code as of that PR.

Primary controller file: internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller.go.

docs.title: PR 1 — ObjectsNotReady (remove ProbeFailure)
docs.text:
• Collapse the in-transition RollingOut branch (:298-299) and the ProbeFailure branch (:367) into a single Ready=False/ObjectsNotReady. Keep the per-object probe detail as the message; fall back to a generic "Objects are not yet ready." before any probe reports. The deadline branch (:361-365) still wins and still summarizes via "Last status".
  • Add ClusterObjectSetReasonObjectsNotReady; remove ClusterObjectSetReasonProbeFailure. COS stops emitting the shared ocv1.ReasonRollingOut.
  • CE: progressingFromReady — map ObjectsNotReady explicitly to Progressing=True/RollingOut (replaces the default/ProbeFailure case); CE Progressing contract (reason RollingOut) is preserved. determineFailureReason needs no change (ObjectsNotReady is not an error reason → Absent).

docs.title: PR 2 — Archiving
docs.text:
• In archive() (:390-409), replace the two teardown-in-progress setRetryableErrorConditions calls (teardown error :394; owned resources not yet removed :398) with Ready=False/Archiving. markAsArchived (→ Archived) stays terminal. The teardown-error path still returns the error for backoff.
  • Add ClusterObjectSetReasonArchiving.
  • CE: Archiving/Archived are archival-path reasons on old revisions; determineFailureReason only inspects the latest rolling revision, so no Failed mapping. Add Archiving to progressingFromReady as neutral (Progressing=True/RollingOut) for completeness.

docs.title: PR 3 — Superseded
docs.text:
• In the not-complete branch, after the ProgressDeadlineExceeded check and before the ObjectsNotReady/probe-detail determination, scan rres.GetPhases() objects for machinery.ActionProgressed. If any (and the deadline is not exceeded), set Ready=False/Superseded with a message naming the superseding direction ("Object(s) have been adopted by a newer revision of the object set."). This honors the precedence ProgressDeadlineExceeded → Superseded → ObjectsNotReady.
  • Siblings are already wired (WithSiblingOwners, :578); boxcutter emits ActionProgressed only for newer-sibling adoption, so no revision comparison is needed on our side.
  • Add ClusterObjectSetReasonSuperseded.
  • CE: Superseded is on the old revision; map to neutral in progressingFromReady; not an error in determineFailureReason.

docs.title: PR 4 — remove RetryableError
docs.text:
• Replace every setRetryableErrorConditions(...) call with: return the wrapped error (controller-runtime requeues with backoff) without mutating Ready. Sites: :153, :176, :193, :219, :229 (and the archive-error path if still present after PR 2). Delete setRetryableErrorConditions and ClusterObjectSetReasonRetryableError.
  • The LifecycleStateArchived TrackingCache.Free error (:207) currently marks RetryableError; switch to returning the error without touching Ready.
  • CE: remove RetryableError from determineFailureReason (:170) and the Retrying branch of progressingFromReady (:276). ObjectCollision stays an error reason in determineFailureReason.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Per PR, extend the existing table tests in internal/object-controller/controllers/clusterobjectset_controller_test.go (status-condition table RevisionReconciliation, collision table ForeignRevisionCollision) and the CE reconstruction tests in internal/operator-controller/controllers/*_test.go. Add e2e scenario updates where the retired reasons are asserted. Verify with make test-unit and make lint each PR; regenerate and commit generated artifacts.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• MutableReferencedSecret / DigestMismatch split from the blueprint — #2985 deliberately consolidated these under ValidationFailure; not reopened here.
  • Message polish beyond what each reason requires (tracked separately).
  • ClusterObjectDeployment layering and moving ProgressDeadlineExceeded off COS (future work once COD lands).
  • Concept-doc Progressing/Succeeded section cleanup beyond the reason rows these PRs touch (pre-existing follow-up).

docs.title: E2E Per-Component Test Suites
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-15 Status: Draft (design) Topic: Reorganize the e2e test suite so each API/component (catalogd, operator-controller, object-controller) is independently testable with its own features, while still supporting a single run across all of them.

docs.title: Problem & Intent
docs.text:
The project has grown three distinct APIs and controllers:

  • catalogd — ClusterCatalog
  • operator-controller — ClusterExtension
  • object-controller — ClusterObjectSet (and soon ClusterObjectDeployment)

Today all e2e tests live in a single Godog (Gherkin/BDD) suite at test/e2e:

  • One entrypoint, test/e2e/features_test.go, globs every *.feature under test/e2e/features/ and runs them together.
  • Features are organized by concern (install, update, status, metrics, namespace, …), not by component. These cut across all three APIs.
  • Step definitions live in a single shared package test/e2e/steps (~5,000 lines total; steps.go alone is ~2,800), consumed by both the e2e suite and test/upgrade-e2e.
  • Selection is driven by --godog.tags and feature paths from the Makefile. Existing tags: @Serial, @demo, @BoxcutterRuntime, @TLSProfile.

Driver (stated): The components may eventually move to separate repositories. We want each component treated as its own thing — independently testable, with its own set of features — while keeping a way to run everything together. This favors physical separation (per-component test packages, features, and suite entrypoints) over logical tag-only separation, because a future repo split should be close to a git mv.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Each component has its own features/ directory and its own suite entrypoint, runnable in isolation.
  • A single command still runs the entire suite across all components.
  • A future repo split is mechanical: move a component directory out; the shared library becomes a vendored/published dependency.
  • No change to test behavior during the reorganization — moves are behavior-preserving.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• True dependency isolation / mocking. These are e2e tests against a real cluster. "Independently testable" means a component's suite can be run on its own and contains the scenarios it owns — not that operator-controller is tested without a real catalogd. The install path legitimately depends on catalogd serving a catalog; that remains an integration reality.
  • Rewriting or changing the semantics of any existing scenario.
  • Introducing new test frameworks. We stay on Godog.

docs.title: Chosen Approach: Directory-per-component + shared library (Approach A)
Target layout
docs.text:
test/e2e/
  shared/                       # extractable library: everything reusable
    world/hooks/helpers         # world state, hooks, "OLM is available", registry + catalog helpers
    runner                      # TestMain boilerplate: options, --e2e.scenario filter, summary wiring
    steps/                      # (post-PR3) truly-shared step definitions
    support-bundle.yaml         # shared diagnostics (moved from test/e2e/)
  operator-controller/
    features/                   # install, update, uninstall, status, namespace, recover, vap-access-control
    suite_test.go               # entrypoint: shared runner + shared steps + OC-specific steps
    steps/                      # (post-PR3) ClusterExtension-specific steps
  catalogd/
    features/                   # ha, proxy, tls
    suite_test.go
    steps/                      # (post-PR3) catalog-specific steps
  object-controller/
    features/                   # revision, user-managed-fields
    suite_test.go
    steps/                      # (post-PR3) COS/COD-specific steps
  platform/                     # genuinely cross-component features
    features/                   # metrics (OC + catalogd), demos
    suite_test.go

Each */suite_test.go is a thin Go test package that calls the shared runner, pointing it at its own features/ directory and registering the shared step set plus any component-specific steps.

docs.title: How "run one" and "run all" work
docs.text:
• Run all: go test ./test/e2e/... — Go's ... wildcard discovers and runs every component subpackage automatically. No tag juggling, no central list to maintain.
  • Run one component: go test ./test/e2e/catalogd/... (etc.).
  • Existing tag-based selection (@Serial serial vs. concurrent, ~@demo exclusion) is preserved within each suite via --godog.tags.

docs.title: Why this over the alternatives
docs.text:
• Tag-only on a single suite (rejected): smallest change, but leaves everything in one package/dir — it does not create the clean boundary a repo split needs, and features are not physically owned. Weakest match to the driver.
  • Hybrid single parameterized runner (rejected): physically separates features/steps but keeps one runner selected by flag. The runner becomes a shared choke point that accretes if component == … conditionals the moment components need different suite-level behavior, and the conversion to per-entrypoint has to happen at split time anyway. We pay the cost later without the clean boundary now.

The expensive work — partitioning features and (eventually) factoring the step library — is identical across these options. Approach A is the only one that makes the repo split mechanical and avoids the shared-runner-conditionals risk, so we do it directly.

docs.title: Cross-Cutting Feature Ownership
docs.text:
Some features are not cleanly owned by a single component. Assignment is by the primary user-facing API under test, with a dedicated platform/ bucket for genuinely cross-component features.

Feature Owner Notes install, update, uninstall, status, namespace, recover, vap-access-control operator-controller Exercise ClusterExtension; catalogd is an assumed dependency, not the subject. revision, user-managed-fields object-controller Already @BoxcutterRuntime. ha, proxy, tls catalogd tls.feature comments confirm all scenarios test catalogd only. All @Serial. metrics platform Single scenario outline tests both operator-controller and catalogd via an Examples table. Splitting would duplicate the scenario; keep as one cross-component feature. demos platform @demo, cross-cutting, already excluded from normal runs via ~@demo. Governed by update-demos.yaml.

Decision: Introduce a platform/ suite for cross-component features rather than forcing metrics/demos into a single owner. The "run all" target (go test ./test/e2e/...) covers it automatically. This is the one design choice most worth confirming on review; the alternative (split metrics per component, drop platform/) is viable but duplicates the metrics scenario.

docs.title: The Shared Library Boundary
docs.text:
test/e2e/shared is the seam a repo split will cut along, so it must hold everything reusable and nothing component-specific:

  • World/state + hooks (hooks.go): scenario setup/teardown, namespace lifecycle.
  • Common Given steps: "OLM is available", "an image registry is available", "a catalog … with packages", generic apply/assert helpers. These are prerequisites every component needs.
  • Runner boilerplate: the Godog Options, the --e2e.scenario prefix filter (findScenarioFirstLineNumberByPrefix), and summary wiring (test/internal/summary) — currently inlined in features_test.go:36-134. Lifted into a shared helper so each suite_test.go is a few lines.
  • Diagnostics: support-bundle.yaml.

test/upgrade-e2e already imports test/e2e/steps; after the move it becomes another consumer of test/e2e/shared/steps. This is expected and reinforces the shared-library design.

docs.title: PR Sequence
docs.text: The ordering is deliberate: PR2 is safe precisely because PR3 has not happened yet. Through PR1–PR2 the step definitions remain one monolithic package, so every component suite can register the entire shared step set. A feature moved into catalogd/features/ still resolves all its steps. Godog Strict: true fails only on undefined/pending steps, never on registered-but-unused ones, so over-registering is free. The step split (PR3) therefore blocks nothing.

docs.title: PR1 — Reroot layout + establish shared (mechanical, behavior-preserving)
docs.text:
• git mv test/e2e/features/ → test/e2e/operator-controller/features/ (all features stay together for now).
  • git mv test/e2e/steps/ → test/e2e/shared/steps/.
  • Lift runner boilerplate (TestMain, --e2e.scenario filter, summary wiring) from features_test.go into test/e2e/shared so later suites reuse it.
  • Create the operator-controller suite_test.go calling the shared runner.
  • Move support-bundle.yaml into shared/.
  • Update all references in the same PR:
  • test/upgrade-e2e/upgrade_test.go import path for the steps package.
  • Makefile targets referencing ./test/e2e/features_test.go (lines ~431, 435, 446, 479, 740) and the e2e/% scenario path.
  • .github/workflows/update-demos.yaml paths (features/demos.feature, steps/demo_steps.go, steps/asciicast_*.go) and the support-bundle.yaml path in e2e.yaml:72.
  • Constraint: no behavior change. The suite still runs the same scenarios; only locations and import paths move.
  • ⚠️ CI workflow edits require maintainer sign-off (per AGENTS.md "never modify .github/workflows/* without explicit permission"). Flag this explicitly in the PR; the demos/support-bundle path updates are unavoidable consequences of the move.

docs.title: PR2 — Sort features into component suites (may split per component)
docs.text:
• Create catalogd/, object-controller/, and platform/ suites, each with a thin suite_test.go that calls the shared runner and registers the full shared step set.
  • git mv features to their owners per the ownership table.
  • The operator-controller suite shrinks as features leave; go test ./test/e2e/... now runs four suites.
  • Can be landed as separate PRs per component (e.g. object-controller first, then catalogd, then platform).
  • Still no step refactor — every suite registers everything, so all steps resolve.

docs.title: PR3 — Split the step library per component (judgment-heavy, incremental)
docs.text:
• Partition shared/steps into truly-shared vs. component-specific. Rough starting map:
  • Shared: hooks.go, world setup, "OLM is available"/registry/catalog Given steps, generic apply/assert (the shared portion of steps.go).
  • operator-controller: ClusterExtension-specific steps from steps.go.
  • catalogd: ha_steps.go, proxy_steps.go, tls_steps.go.
  • platform/demos: demo_steps.go, asciicast_hooks.go, asciicast_recorder.go.
  • upgrade-e2e: upgrade_steps.go (consider relocating to the upgrade suite).
  • Each suite registers shared + its own steps.
  • Can land one component at a time; nothing depends on it completing. This is where a future repo split becomes trivial.

docs.title: Sequencing summary
docs.text: PR Scope Risk Splittable PR1 Reroot + shared, update refs Low (mechanical) No PR2 Sort features into suites Low (moves; over-registered steps) Up to 3–4 PRs PR3 Split step library Medium (judgment) Up to 3–4 PRs, incremental

docs.title: Testing & Verification
docs.text:
• Each PR: make test-e2e (and make test-experimental-e2e for object-controller / @BoxcutterRuntime features) must stay green. Because PR1–PR2 are behavior-preserving moves, the same scenario set runs with the same pass/fail.
  • Run-all: verify go test ./test/e2e/... discovers and runs every component suite.
  • Run-one: verify go test ./test/e2e/<component>/... runs only that component's features.
  • Tag behavior: confirm @Serial scenarios still run serially and ~@demo exclusion still applies within each suite.
  • upgrade-e2e: confirm it still builds and runs after the steps package moves.
  • make verify / make lint for import and formatting correctness.

docs.title: Open Decisions (for review)
docs.text:
1. platform/ bucket vs. splitting metrics/demos per component. Recommended: keep platform/. Alternative: duplicate the metrics scenario outline per component and drop platform/.
  2. Per-component Makefile targets. Whether to add test-e2e-<component> convenience targets, or rely on go test ./test/e2e/<component>/... directly. (Leaning: add thin targets mirroring the existing test-e2e env setup, since cluster/manifest env wiring is non-trivial.)
  3. upgrade_steps.go home. Relocate into the upgrade suite during PR3, or keep in shared/steps.

docs.title: Design: Separate object-controller into its own downstream component
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-19 Status: Draft design (pre-plan) Author: Per G. da Silva (with Claude)

docs.title: 1. Intent and why
docs.text:
Downstream (OpenShift), the object-controller (the ClusterObjectSet / boxcutter runtime manager) is currently a passenger: its binary is baked into the ose-olm-operator-controller payload image, and its workload is rendered into the openshift-operator-controller namespace as part of the operator-controller Helm render. This was done to avoid breaking CI while the component stabilized.

We want object-controller to be a first-class downstream component, on the same footing as catalogd and operator-controller:

  • Its own payload image (ose-olm-object-controller).
  • Its own namespace (openshift-object-controller).
  • Deployed only when the BoxcutterRuntime feature gate is enabled (TechPreview).

The hard constraint is CI must stay green at every merge, in every repo. It is acceptable to pass through intermediate states where the binary still exists in the operator-controller image, or where the component still installs into openshift-operator-controller, as long as each individual merge is additive or atomic and leaves CI green. A final cleanup PR after the cross-over is explicitly in scope.

docs.title: Key reframing discovered during investigation
docs.text:
Upstream (operator-framework/operator-controller, this repo) is already fully split. The object-controller already has its own cmd/object-controller binary, its own Dockerfile.object-controller, its own .goreleaser.yml entries, its own internal/object-controller/ tree, and its own Helm templates (gated by the objectController.enabled helper in _helpers.tpl). Upstream deploys everything into the single namespaces.olmv1.name namespace, which is correct and desirable for upstream.

Therefore the bundling lives entirely in the downstream openshift/ carry (openshift/operator-framework-operator-controller), not upstream. The bulk of this work is in three places: the downstream fork, openshift/ocp-build-data, and openshift/cluster-olm-operator. Upstream needs only two small, backward- compatible Helm _helpers.tpl changes plus a smoke test and a docs update.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• object-controller ships as its own OpenShift payload image built from the downstream fork, mirroring how catalogd and operator-controller images are built.
  • object-controller is deployed into openshift-object-controller and only when BoxcutterRuntime is enabled.
  • cluster-olm-operator renders object-controller as a third, first-class component with its own image env var, image-references entry, manifest copy initContainer, namespace, and RBAC readiness waits.
  • A clean final cleanup that removes the object-controller binary from the operator-controller image and removes the object-controller passenger block from the operator-controller Helm values.
  • CI stays green at every individual merge in every repo.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• No scoped RBAC in this effort. object-controller keeps its current binding to the built-in cluster-admin ClusterRole. A least-privilege ClusterRole is a separate follow-up.
  • No change to upstream's single-namespace (olmv1-system) layout. Upstream continues to deploy all three controllers into one namespace.
  • No change to the BoxcutterRuntime gate semantics or to when the feature is considered TechPreview.
  • No new git repository. Like catalogd and operator-controller, the new component is a new image built from the single downstream fork openshift/operator-framework-operator-controller; it is not a new source repo.

docs.title: Anti-goals (would make this a failure even if it "works")
docs.text:
• Any merge that leaves a repo's CI red, requiring a follow-up "fixup" to go green.
  • A window in which object-controller is deployed twice (once in openshift-operator-controller via the old passenger path and once in openshift-object-controller via the new path) — object collisions / double reconciliation. (See §6.5: on fresh installs this cannot happen; it would only arise on an upgrade across the change, which the feature-set semantics forbid.)
  • A window in which cluster-olm-operator references the new operand image (env var, image-references, or manifest-copy initContainer) before that image is actually built and available in the CI payload — the operator pod would fail to start.
  • Any destructive handoff of the ClusterObjectSet CRD that could cascade-delete live ClusterObjectSet CRs. (See §6.5: verified not to happen — apply-only.)

docs.title: Upstream (this repo) — already separated
docs.text:
• Binary: cmd/object-controller/main.go (own main, leader-election lock object-controller-lock.olm.operatorframework.io).
  • Image: Dockerfile.object-controller → object-controller:<tag>; dedicated .goreleaser.yml build + docker-manifest entries; make docker-build builds it separately.
  • Implementation: internal/object-controller/; API api/v1/clusterobjectset_types.go.
  • Helm: Deployment, Service, PDB, ServiceMonitor, NetworkPolicy, cert, RBAC (ClusterRoleBinding to cluster-admin), and CRD — all gated by the objectController.enabled helper (helm/olmv1/templates/_helpers.tpl:67-87).
  • Gate helper behavior:
  • $boxcutterEnabled = operatorController.enabled AND BoxcutterRuntime in operatorController.features.enabled AND NOT in .disabled.
  • objectController.enabled null → defaults to $boxcutterEnabled.
  • Explicit true is allowed ("Set true to deploy independently").
  • Fails if objectController.enabled is explicitly false while boxcutter is enabled (_helpers.tpl:74-76).
  • Fails unless options.featureSet == experimental (_helpers.tpl:82-84).
  • Namespace: single namespaces.olmv1.name for all three controllers.

docs.title: Downstream fork (operator-framework-operator-controller, the openshift/ carry)
docs.text:
• Uses the upstream helm/olmv1 chart verbatim (COPY'd into each image, not vendored). Downstream customization is expressed only through external values files.
  • openshift/operator-controller.Dockerfile copies both /operator-controller and /object-controller binaries into the one image (comment: "object-controller is baked into this image for now"). Also copies openshift/operator-controller/cp-manifests, helm/olmv1, experimental.yaml, and operator-controller.yaml (renamed to openshift.yaml in the image).
  • openshift/catalogd.Dockerfile copies catalogd only, plus catalogd's cp-manifests, chart, and catalogd.yaml→openshift.yaml.
  • openshift/helm/operator-controller.yaml: namespaces.olmv1.name: openshift-operator-controller, operatorController.enabled: true, objectController block present with no enabled key (null → follows the boxcutter gate) and objectController.deployment.image: ${OPERATOR_CONTROLLER_IMAGE}, catalogd.enabled: false, openshift.enabled: true, featureSet: standard.
  • openshift/helm/catalogd.yaml: namespaces.olmv1.name: openshift-catalogd, catalogd.enabled: true, operatorController.enabled: false.
  • openshift/helm/experimental.yaml: overlay; featureSet: experimental; currently lists BoxcutterRuntime in the DISABLED list — so with the shipped values object-controller does not render; cluster-olm-operator overrides BoxcutterRuntime on when the OpenShift gate is enabled.
  • cp-manifests is a per-component shell script copying /openshift/helm/* into ${dest}/helm/<component>/. openshift/helm/generate-manifests.sh produces per-component snapshot manifests for diff verification.
  • No object-controller.Dockerfile, no openshift/object-controller/ dir, no openshift/helm/object-controller.yaml.

docs.title: ocp-build-data (branches openshift-4.20, openshift-4.21)
docs.text:
• images/ose-olm-operator-controller.yml and images/ose-olm-catalogd.yml: both for_payload: true, built from the downstream fork via openshift/<name>.Dockerfile, payload_name: olm-operator-controller / olm-catalogd, distgit rhaos-{MAJOR}.{MINOR}-rhel-9.
  • No ose-olm-object-controller.yml.

docs.title: cluster-olm-operator
docs.text:
• Renders operand charts in-process with the Helm SDK (pkg/controller/helm.go), from charts copied into /operand-assets by initContainers (copy-catalogd-manifests, copy-operator-controller-manifests in manifests/0000_51_olm_06_deployment.yaml) that run each operand image's cp-manifests.
  • Renders only two components: cb.BuildControllers("catalogd", "operator-controller") (cmd/cluster-olm-operator/main.go:384). object-controller rides inside the operator-controller render.
  • Image injection (helm.go:78-91): options.catalogd.deployment.image ← CATALOGD_IMAGE; options.operatorController.deployment.image ← OPERATOR_CONTROLLER_IMAGE; options.objectController.deployment.image ← OPERATOR_CONTROLLER_IMAGE (same env var — reuses the operator-controller image).
  • Feature-gate mapping (internal/featuregates/mapper.go): OpenShift FeatureGateNewOLMBoxCutterRuntime → upstream BoxcutterRuntime on operator-controller; applied to helm values by pkg/controller/featuregates_hook.go.
  • manifests/image-references lists 4 images (cluster-olm-operator, olm-catalogd, olm-operator-controller, kube-rbac-proxy). No object-controller.
  • Namespaces: operator's own ns is openshift-cluster-olm-operator; operand namespaces come from operand chart values. The only hardcoded operand ns in Go is operatorControllerNamespace = "openshift-operator-controller" (main.go:53). object-controller shares it.
  • Detection/readiness: objectControllerRendered() (main.go:341-348) checks for the object-controller SA in openshift-operator-controller; waitForOLMv1ComponentsRBAC then waits for its SA + object-controller-cluster-admin-rolebinding.
  • HA overrides (helm.go:102-127) already cover options.objectController.deployment.replicas / podDisruptionBudget.enabled.

docs.title: Verified cluster-olm-operator runtime behavior (apply/prune)
docs.text:
Confirmed against the cluster-olm-operator source; this is the foundation of the crossover-safety argument in §6.5. - Apply-only, never prune. Each component gets its own library-go StaticResourceController built with the plain constructor (no WithConditionalResources), so the delete path is unreachable (shouldDelete is always false). Resources that disappear from a render are neither applied nor deleted — they linger. - Per-component, independent. BuildControllers("catalogd", "operator-controller") builds one controller set per component; there is no combined aggregate set and no diff against prior cluster state. - The operand CRDs (ClusterObjectSet, ClusterExtension, ClusterCatalog) are rendered by the operand Helm charts (copied from the operand images into /operand-assets) and applied apply-only via the per-component StaticResourceController. cluster-olm-operator never deletes a CRD it applied. (The only CRD baked into the cluster-olm-operator image itself is its own operator.openshift.io OLMConfig CRD, applied by the CVO.) - relatedObjects is informational only — used for informer namespaces, ClusterOperator status/must-gather, and the object-controller readiness check. It is never used to prune. The only Delete calls in the whole operator are a hardcoded legacy-RBAC cleanup (cleanupOldOperatorControllerRBAC), never CRDs or workloads. - Re-render happens by process restart (on feature-gate/topology change); the manifest set is fixed per process lifetime.

Consequence: moving a resource (including the ClusterObjectSet CRD) from one render to another is additive and non-destructive — the new component applies it; the old component ceasing to render it deletes nothing.

docs.title: 4. Target end state
docs.text:
• ose-olm-object-controller is a for_payload: true image built from openshift/object-controller.Dockerfile in the downstream fork, listed in cluster-olm-operator image-references.
  • The downstream fork has openshift/object-controller.Dockerfile (copies only /object-controller), openshift/object-controller/cp-manifests, and openshift/helm/object-controller.yaml with namespaces.olmv1.name: openshift-object-controller.
  • cluster-olm-operator renders three components: BuildControllers("catalogd", "operator-controller", "object-controller"). The object-controller render targets openshift-object-controller, takes its image from a new OBJECT_CONTROLLER_IMAGE env var, has a copy-object-controller-manifests initContainer, and its own namespace + RBAC readiness waits.
  • object-controller is excluded from the operator-controller render.
  • The operator-controller image no longer carries the object-controller binary; operator-controller.yaml no longer carries the objectController block.
  • object-controller deploys only when BoxcutterRuntime (TechPreview) is on; default (non-TechPreview) clusters deploy nothing new.
  • RBAC unchanged (still cluster-admin).

docs.title: 5. Constraints and decisions (locked)
docs.text:
1. CI-safe at every merge. Every merge is either strictly additive, or an atomic cross-over that updates producers and consumers together.
  2. RBAC: keep cluster-admin. No scoped ClusterRole in this effort.
  3. ART/payload onboarding is an external prerequisite, captured here as a checklist and sequenced first; we edit the ocp-build-data config and the cluster-olm-operator references, but the ART approval/distgit/CVP steps are driven out-of-band by the author.
  4. Downstream fork is the primary code repo for this work. Upstream change is limited to two small, backward-compatible _helpers.tpl tweaks, one smoke render, and a docs update.
  5. No double-deploy window and no dangling-image-reference window (see anti-goals).
  6. No installed base to migrate. BoxcutterRuntime is TechPreview/CI-only with no upgrade guarantee (confirmed). It is reachable only via *NoUpgrade feature sets (TechPreviewNoUpgrade / CustomNoUpgrade / DevPreviewNoUpgrade), which block cluster upgrades. Therefore every cluster that receives the new layout is a fresh install, and no cluster carries the old object-controller layout across an upgrade.
  7. Derived constraint — land before GA. The separation must land while BoxcutterRuntime is still pre-GA (not promoted to Default). Once it is on by default, a real installed base exists and a destructive migration would be required. Completing the split while it is TechPreview makes migration a non-issue forever (fresh GA installs get the new layout from day one).

docs.title: 6. The minimal upstream foundation (this repo)
docs.text:
These must be backward-compatible: existing standard/experimental renders (and their checked-in manifests/*.yaml) must be byte-for-byte unchanged so upstream CI stays green.

U1 — Decouple object-controller enablement from operator-controller in helm/olmv1/templates/_helpers.tpl. Two problems block a clean separation: - The standalone object-controller render (operatorController disabled) can never turn object-controller on, because $boxcutterEnabled requires operatorController.enabled. - The operator-controller render cannot exclude object-controller when boxcutter is on, because setting objectController.enabled: false while boxcutter is enabled makes the helper fail (_helpers.tpl:74-76).

The fix must preserve current default behavior (null + operator-controller + boxcutter → object-controller renders in the same namespace, as upstream does today) while additionally allowing: - an explicit objectController.enabled: false to suppress object-controller even when boxcutter is on (relax/remove the fail-on-false guard), and - a standalone render where objectController.enabled: true (operatorController disabled) renders cleanly under featureSet: experimental.

The builder should choose the least-invasive helper refactor that satisfies both and keeps all existing rendered manifests unchanged. (Candidate: keep the null→$boxcutterEnabled default, drop the fail-on-false guard, and confirm the explicit-true standalone path renders.)

U2 — Standalone-render smoke test. Add a render-only smoke check to make manifests (alongside the existing openshift.enabled=true and tilt smoke renders) that renders the chart with only objectController enabled, openshift.enabled=true, featureSet=experimental, and a distinct namespaces.olmv1.name, to lock the standalone render in CI. Verify the shared ServiceAccount template, the component.name.prefix / olmv1.label.name helpers, namespace creation, and ServiceMonitor all behave with only object-controller present.

U3 — Docs. Update docs/draft/concepts/clusterobjectsets.md (and any api-reference prose) to describe object-controller as a separate downstream image/namespace rather than a passenger in the operator-controller image.

U1/U2/U3 are additive and backward-compatible → one upstream PR, CI stays green. They flow downstream via the normal rebase/carry, so the updated chart is baked into rebuilt operand images before the cross-over.

docs.title: 6.5 Crossover safety analysis (the decisive argument)
docs.text:
The §2 anti-goals (no double-deploy, no destructive CRD handoff) are satisfied by the combination of three verified facts:

  1. Apply-only runtime (§3). No render ever prunes. Moving the ClusterObjectSet CRD and the object-controller workload from the operator-controller render to the object-controller render is additive: the new component applies them; nothing deletes the old render's objects.
  2. Fresh installs only (constraint 6). Because BoxcutterRuntime is only reachable on *NoUpgrade clusters, which cannot upgrade, there is never a running cluster that already has object-controller in openshift-operator-controller and then transitions to the new layout. On a fresh install of the post-crossover payload, the old-namespace object-controller objects are never created in the first place — so the "lingering old workload → double reconciliation" scenario cannot occur.
  3. Atomic consumer flip (Phase 3b). The single cluster-olm-operator change both enables the object-controller render and excludes object-controller from the operator-controller render, so even within one process there is exactly one object-controller workload.

CRD ownership after the split. The object-controller component owns the ClusterObjectSet CRD render (it is gated by objectController.enabled). The operator-controller workload, when BoxcutterRuntime is on, creates ClusterObjectSet CRs and therefore depends on that CRD existing. Because (a) static-resource controllers start before the Deployment controllers (CRD-apply precedes the workloads), and (b) the operator-controller workload retries CR creation until the CRD is present, this is eventually consistent and low-risk. If the builder wants to eliminate even the transient race, the CRD may additionally be rendered by a stable component (apply-only makes double-rendering a harmless idempotent re-apply) — but this is an optional hardening, not a requirement.

Residual (out-of-scope) risk. The only scenario that would reintroduce the double-deploy risk is an in-place upgrade of a cluster that had the old layout — which the feature-set semantics forbid today. This is explicitly out of scope per constraint 6, and is permanently avoided by landing the split before GA (constraint 7). A best-effort cleanup of the old-namespace object-controller objects (mirroring the existing cleanupOldOperatorControllerRBAC pattern) is included as optional hygiene in Phase 4 for dev clusters that manually toggled the gate — it is not required for correctness.

docs.title: 7. Phased, CI-safe migration plan
docs.text: Phases are ordered by dependency. Each phase is green-on-merge.

docs.title: Phase 0 — ART / payload onboarding (external prerequisite, start first)
docs.text:
Longest lead time; begin immediately and in parallel. - Create the distgit / delivery plumbing for a new payload image ose-olm-object-controller (openshift4/ose-olm-object-controller-rhel9, payload_name: olm-object-controller), mirroring ose-olm-operator-controller.yml. - Secure ART approval to add a new payload image to the OCP release payload for the target release branch(es).

Hard ordering dependencies (do not violate — these break the nightly): - The openshift/object-controller.Dockerfile must already exist on the targeted downstream release-X.Y branch(es) before the ocp-build-data image config builds.
